cheapest-golf-near-albufeira.text: Looking for the **cheapest golf near Albufeira**? You don't have to go far. Albufeira has two short 9-hole courses, and a full 18-hole course 17 minutes from the old town starts at **€78**. This guide compares green fees at every course within about half an hour, and shows which one is cheapest depending on whether you want nine holes, eighteen, or a buggy included.

Prices are the lowest visitor green fee for one round, from each club's official price list or its own online booking for the 2026/27 season, checked in October 2026. Drive times are from Albufeira old town, without traffic. This isn't a complete list, and prices change, so always check when you book.
Green fees near Albufeira compared

cheapest-golf-near-albufeira.text: The cheapest 18-hole round: Salgados

[Salgados](/courses/salgados), behind Praia da Galé, is the cheapest full course near Albufeira. It costs **€78** in January, July and August, €102 in February, March and June, and up to €139 in spring and autumn. Its twilight rate is cheaper still: **€47** in those same three months.
It's also flat, and Where2Golf says players generally walk it, so you can skip the €50 buggy if you're happy on foot. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies.
The cheapest round with a buggy: Amendoeira

If you want a buggy, [Amendoeira](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) near Silves can work out cheaper than Salgados. Its online green fee of **€100** in December and January includes a buggy if one is available. In January, a round at Salgados plus its €50 buggy comes to €128 for one player. From June to August, Amendoeira costs €109 with the buggy, against €128 at Salgados with a buggy in July and August. Both of Amendoeira's courses, the Faldo and the O'Connor, have the same rates.
The cheapest short rounds

**[Balaia](/courses/balaia)** is a 9-hole par-3 course at Balaia Golf Village, 13 minutes from the old town. Its 2025/26 price list shows a **€50 day fee**. The resort asks for a handicap but doesn't publish a limit.

**[Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs)** sits on the cliffs above Praia da Falésia, 18 minutes away. Nine holes cost **€57** for most of the year and €76 in February to May and October. Players without a handicap can play from the red tees, which makes it the easiest place near Albufeira to start. Our [Balaia vs Pine Cliffs](/guide/balaia-vs-pine-cliffs-which-quick-round-near-albufeira-should-you-play) guide compares the two.
Cheapest golf near Albufeira for beginners

Start at Pine Cliffs if you don't have a handicap yet. Once you do, [Vilamoura Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium), 24 minutes away, is a forgiving 18-hole course from €88, and Salgados is a flat, walkable option from €78. See [the best Algarve golf courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners) for more.
Frequently asked questions
What is the cheapest golf course near Albufeira?
For a full 18 holes, Salgados, from €78 in January, July and August, or €47 at twilight. For a short round, Balaia's €50 day fee or nine holes at Pine Cliffs from €57.
Can you play golf in Albufeira without a handicap?
Yes, at Pine Cliffs, from the red tees. Balaia and Salgados both ask for a handicap.
When is golf cheapest near Albufeira?

January, July and August at Salgados, and December and January at Amendoeira. Spring and autumn are the most expensive months at most courses. Our [Algarve golf season guide](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf) explains why.

For all the courses on a map, see [Albufeira golf courses](/albufeira/golf-courses). Planning the whole trip? Read [how much a golf trip to Albufeira costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-albufeira-cost) and how to get from [Faro Airport to Albufeira with golf clubs](/guide/faro-airport-to-albufeira-with-golf-clubs).

cheapest-golf-in-vilamoura.text: Vilamoura is one of the Algarve's best-known golf resorts, but it isn't one of the cheapest places to play. The lowest green fee in Vilamoura itself is **€88**, and the famous Old Course starts at €215. This guide shows the **cheapest golf in Vilamoura** course by course, when to go for the lowest prices, and the cheaper rounds a short drive away.

Prices are the lowest visitor green fee for one round, taken from each club's official price list or its own online booking for the 2026/27 season and checked in October 2026. Drive times are from Vilamoura marina, without traffic. This isn't a complete list of every option, and prices change, so always check when you book.
Vilamoura green fees compared

Five courses in Vilamoura take visitors: the four run by Vilamoura Golf (Laguna, Millennium, Pinhal and the Old Course) and Pestana's Vila Sol. Vilamoura Golf's fifth course, the Els Club, is a private members' club and can't be booked by visitors.

cheapest-golf-in-vilamoura.text: [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) are the cheapest courses in Vilamoura. Both cost €97 in July and August, and drop to €88 in late autumn: in November at Laguna and in December at Millennium. The dearest months are February to May, at €132 to €136, and Laguna is also €136 in January.
Laguna's free buggy offer

Vilamoura Golf doesn't publish a buggy hire price, so a free buggy makes a real difference. Its **Laguna on Wheels** offer gives a complimentary shared buggy on every round at Laguna for new bookings made by 31 December 2026, for play from 19 October 2026 to 31 December 2027. It isn't valid from 1 April to 31 May or from 16 September to 18 October 2027. That makes Laguna the cheapest way we found to play a full round in Vilamoura with a buggy.
Vila Sol: twilight and two-player deals

[Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol) starts at €140, but it has two ways to pay less. Its twilight rate is **€60** from 3:30pm all year, with a twilight buggy at €40. And Pestana's summer special for two players sharing a buggy costs €208 from June to August, which is **€104 each** with the buggy included, or €300 for two from 16 to 30 May and in September. See our guide to [best value golf in the Algarve](/guide/best-value-golf-in-the-algarve) for the full Pestana deal.

cheapest-golf-in-vilamoura.text: [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) is a 9-hole clifftop course above Praia da Falésia, from €57 for nine holes, and players without a handicap can play from the red tees. [Balaia](/courses/balaia) is a 9-hole par-3 course with a €50 day fee; it asks for a handicap but doesn't publish a limit.

For a full 18 holes, [Vale do Lobo](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean)'s Sunset rate starts at **€76** in January, February, November and December, and the club includes a shared buggy for full-paying adults on that rate. That's cheaper than a standard round at any course in Vilamoura. Further west, [Salgados](/courses/salgados) costs from €78, with twilight rounds from €47, but it's about 43 minutes from Vilamoura by car.
The cheapest Vilamoura course for beginners

[Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) is the one we'd suggest for newer golfers: it has wide fairways, it's described as flat, and it has the lowest official slope rating of Vilamoura Golf's four courses (130 from the back tees, against 135 to 140 for the others). [Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) costs the same, but its water carries make it harder for a beginner.

All the Vilamoura courses ask for a handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. If you don't have one yet, Pine Cliffs is the nearest course where you can play without a handicap. Our guides to [the best Algarve courses for beginners](/guide/the-10-best-algarve-golf-courses-for-beginners) and [handicap rules in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) have more.
How to pay less for golf in Vilamoura

**Pick your month.** July and August cost €97 at both Laguna and Millennium, and the lowest prices come in November at Laguna and December at Millennium (€88). The dearest months are March to May at the Old Course and Pinhal, and February to May at Laguna and Millennium.
**Choose Laguna if you want a buggy.** The Laguna on Wheels offer is the clearest saving in Vilamoura while it runs.
**Play late or as a pair at Vila Sol.** Its €60 twilight rate and the two-player summer deal both cut the price well below its standard green fee.
Frequently asked questions
What is the cheapest golf course in Vilamoura?
Laguna and Millennium, both from €88: in November at Laguna and in December at Millennium. In summer, both cost €97.
Is golf in Vilamoura expensive?

Compared with the rest of the Algarve, yes. The cheapest 18-hole round in Vilamoura is €88, while the cheapest in the Algarve start at €57 to €67, mainly in the far west and east. See [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve) for the full list, and [how much a golf trip to Vilamoura costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost) for a whole-trip budget.
Is there cheap golf near Vilamoura without a handicap?
Pine Cliffs, 25 minutes away, lets players without a handicap play from the red tees, with nine holes from €57.

For every course, price and handicap rule side by side, see [Vilamoura golf courses](/vilamoura/golf-courses) on our map. If you're still choosing where to stay, our guide to [golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura) can help.

algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-go.text: Golf in the Algarve is a year-round sport. The courses never shut for a season the way they do in northern Europe, and you can tee off in shorts in January nearly as easily as in July. But the golf season in the Algarve still has a rhythm: green fees at many courses are a third or more lower in the cheapest months than at peak, hotels fill and empty with the beach crowd rather than the golf crowd, and the weather shifts from warm-and-dry to short-and-showery and back again. This month-by-month guide covers what to expect on the course, in your hotel and in your wallet across the whole year, then names the months that give you the best balance.

Two patterns are worth holding in mind before the detail. First, green fees peak in spring and autumn (roughly March to May and October) and bottom out in mid-summer and mid-winter. Pestana's published rates, for example, run about €95 in the low season against €180 at peak for its Carvoeiro courses. Second, hotel prices and crowds follow the opposite curve: they are highest in July and August, when Algarve golf is actually at its quietest, and lowest from November to February, when some resort hotels cut back service or close for a few weeks.
Playing golf in the Algarve in January

January is the quietest and cheapest month of the year. Fairways can be soft after winter rain and a handful of courses take a short maintenance break, but tee sheets are wide open and you can often walk on. Green fees are at their lowest, and rooms are cheap where hotels are open, though choice is limited because some resorts stay closed until February. Days are short, so book a late-morning tee time and you will still finish comfortably before dark. Bright, still mornings are common, and the rain that does come tends to arrive in bands of a day or two rather than constant drizzle.
**Quick numbers:** highs around 16°C, lows around 8°C. About 10 hours of daylight. About six rainy days and 49 mm of rain. Read the full [January guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-january).
Playing golf in the Algarve in February

February is still low season for green fees on most courses, but conditions start to turn. Rainfall eases, the daylight lengthens noticeably and the almond blossom is out. Courses get busy only around the UK half-term week, when families arrive; outside that week you will find space and value. More hotels reopen than in January, widening your choice. This is one of the best-value windows of the year, as long as you accept that an afternoon shower is still possible and the greens are not yet at their spring pace.

**Quick numbers:** highs around 17°C, lows around 9°C. About 11 hours of daylight. About five rainy days and 42 mm of rain, the driest month of the winter. Read the full [February guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-february).
Playing golf in the Algarve in March

In March the season steps up. Courses fill out as spring golf packages begin and Easter approaches, and green fees move into the peak band on many courses. The trade-off is some of the year's best playing weather: warm afternoons, long-enough days and grass growing back into the fairways. Hotels raise their rates but are not yet full. Book tee times and rooms well ahead for the Easter fortnight, which is the single busiest stretch of spring.

**Quick numbers:** highs around 19°C, lows around 11°C. About 12 hours of daylight. About six rainy days and 47 mm of rain, usually in short spells. Read the full [March guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-march).
Playing golf in the Algarve in April

April is peak season in full swing and, for many golfers, the best all-round month to play. Days are long, afternoons are reliably warm without being hot, the rough is green and the courses are in excellent shape. It is also one of the busiest and most expensive months: green fees are at or near their annual high, popular courses book out days ahead and hotel rates are firm. If April is your window, reserve everything early and consider the quieter east or west ends of the region.
**Quick numbers:** highs around 21°C, lows around 12°C. About 13 hours of daylight. About five rainy days and 39 mm of rain. Read the full [April guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-april).
Playing golf in the Algarve in May

May is arguably the peak of the golf calendar. The weather is close to ideal, dry and warm with a very low rain risk, and the courses are busy, with green fees at or near their spring peak. Hotels are busy, but the school-holiday surge has not yet arrived, so rooms are easier to find than in July. Book tee times ahead, and aim for morning slots as the days warm up.
**Quick numbers:** highs around 23–24°C, lows around 15°C. About 14 hours of daylight. About four rainy days and 26 mm of rain. Read the full [May guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-may).
Playing golf in the Algarve in June

June is the pivot month. Green fees drop back into the low-season band as the heat builds, yet the golf is still very good if you tee off early, and course traffic thins through the month. Hotels move the other way, climbing toward their summer peak as the beach season opens and the first school holidays begin, so you may pay less for golf and more for your room than you would in April. Daylight is at its maximum, which makes early and twilight tee times genuinely comfortable. The west of the region is noticeably cooler than the centre and east from June onwards.

**Quick numbers:** highs around 27°C, lows around 18°C. Nearly 15 hours of daylight, the longest of the year. Usually no more than one rainy day, and about five days above 30°C in Faro. Read the full [June guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-june).
Playing golf in the Algarve in July

July is hot, dry and quiet on the course. Along with mid-winter, July and August are the cheapest months for green fees, and tee sheets stay open because most visitors are on the beach rather than the fairway. Play at dawn or from late afternoon; the middle of the day is uncomfortable and hard on your scorecard. Hotels are the opposite story, full and expensive with UK, Irish and Portuguese school holidays all overlapping. Book accommodation months ahead, then enjoy the pick of tee times once you arrive. It runs hotter inland, around [Silves](/courses/silves) for example, and cooler in the far west.

**Quick numbers:** highs around 29°C, lows around 20°C, with about 13 days above 30°C in Faro. About 14.5 hours of daylight. Effectively no rain. The far west is cooler, at around 25°C. Read the full [July guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-july).
Playing golf in the Algarve in August

August is much like July: low green fees, quiet courses, packed and pricey hotels. The heat is the main obstacle, so this is a month for buggies, early alarms and plenty of water. Courses are well irrigated and stay green, though summer greens are slower than spring ones. If you can find a room at a sensible price, August is a cheap month to play a lot of golf around a family beach holiday.

**Quick numbers:** highs around 29°C, lows around 20°C, with about 12 days above 30°C in Faro. About 13.5 hours of daylight. Almost no rain. The far west is cooler, at around 26°C. Read the full [August guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-august).
Playing golf in the Algarve in September

For many golfers September is the best month of all. The extreme heat fades, the sea is at its warmest, rain is still rare and the beach crowds thin once UK schools go back at the start of the month. Green fees climb back towards their autumn peak, and hotel rates ease from their August peak. Early September gives you summer weather at shoulder prices; late September gives you near-perfect golfing conditions as the peak autumn window opens.
**Quick numbers:** highs around 26°C, lows around 18°C. About 12.5 hours of daylight. About two rainy days and 22 mm of rain. Read the full [September guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-september).
Playing golf in the Algarve in October

October is the autumn peak. Courses are extremely busy and green fees are at or close to their annual high as northern Europe escapes the cold. The weather is usually excellent early in the month, still warm and mostly dry, though the first serious rain of the season can arrive. Some courses overseed their fairways now, which can mean temporary greens or minor disruption. Book tee times and hotels as far ahead as you can, because October sells out early.

**Quick numbers:** highs around 23°C, lows around 16°C. About 11 hours of daylight, dropping fast once the clocks go back at the end of the month. About six rainy days and 56 mm of rain. Read the full [October guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-october).
Playing golf in the Algarve in November

In November the season winds down. Green fees fall back to mid-season on most courses, and lower still late in the month, and the courses are quiet again. Weather is the gamble: you can get a run of warm, calm, blue-sky days or a week of Atlantic fronts, and November is statistically one of the wettest months. Fairways soften. Hotels are cheap and some begin to close for winter. Good value for flexible golfers who will take the weather as it comes.

**Quick numbers:** highs around 20°C, lows around 12°C. About 10 hours of daylight. About seven rainy days and 76 mm of rain, and in the far west November is the wettest month of the year. Read the full [November guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-november).
Playing golf in the Algarve in December

Along with January, December is the quietest and cheapest month. Green fees are at their lowest, courses are near empty and you can often book same-day. It is also the wettest month on average and the darkest, with under 10 hours of daylight, so tee times cluster around the middle of the day. A few courses close briefly for maintenance and some hotels shut until February, though the Christmas and New Year week is a small exception, with a short spike in demand and prices.

**Quick numbers:** highs around 17°C, lows around 10°C. About 9.5 hours of daylight, the shortest of the year. About seven rainy days and 90 mm of rain, the most of any month in Faro. Read the full [December guide](/guide/algarve-golf-in-december).
The best months to play golf in the Algarve

If you want the best conditions and don't mind paying for them, play from late April into May or from late September into October. You get long days, warm and dry weather and courses in top shape, against the highest green fees of the year, the fullest tee sheets and firm hotel rates. Book months ahead.

For the best value with still-reliable weather, look at June, November or late January into February. Green fees are noticeably below their peak, the courses are quieter and the weather is usually good enough, with the trade-offs of summer heat in June, a real chance of rain in November and short days in winter.

For the cheapest golf, play in June, July or August. Green fees are as low as they get and the courses are quiet, but you have to tee off early to beat the heat and you will pay peak prices for a busy hotel. Mid-winter, December and January, is just as cheap for both golf and rooms, with the trade-off of short days, soft fairways and the highest rain risk of the year.

In short: spring and autumn for conditions, winter for a bargain, high summer for empty fairways if you can handle the heat. The quietest tee sheets of all are in December, January, July and August. When you have picked your month, you can compare courses, green fees and nearby hotels on the [interactive map](/).
**Fancy a competition?** See our guide to [golf tournaments in the Algarve](/guide/golf-tournaments-in-the-algarve), with amateur events you can enter from December to May.

**Staying for the winter?** Our guide to [long-stay golf in the Algarve](/guide/long-stay-golf-in-the-algarve) compares short-term memberships, round packages and golf societies, and explains how long EU and UK visitors can stay.

gramacho-vs-vale-da-pinta-which-pestana-.text: Gramacho and Vale da Pinta sit inside the same Pestana resort near Carvoeiro, opened within a year of each other in the early '90s, and share the same architect. Ask around locally, though, and most golfers will tell you the same thing: one of them is the crowd-pleaser, the other is the one serious players ask for by name.
One resort, one designer, a year apart

**Ronald Fream** designed both courses for the Pestana Carvoeiro resort — Gramacho first, opening in 1991 with later input from world number one golfer **Nick Price**, followed by Vale da Pinta in 1992. Both weave through the rocky, wooded terrain typical of this stretch of coast, but the two courses feel genuinely different to play.

Gramacho plays 6,107 metres par 72 and has a genuine design quirk: it's built with 18 fairways but **27 greens**, meaning several holes can be played into a completely different green depending on the day, changing the approach shot each time. It's hosted the Portuguese Ladies Open on multiple occasions, and centuries-old carob, almond and olive trees line the fairways alongside artfully placed lakes and bunkers. It's considered the more approachable of the two, well suited to resort golfers rather than just low handicappers.
Stay inside the resort at [Pestana Gramacho Residences](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pestana-gramacho-residences.html), a golf aparthotel 500 metres from the clubhouse.
Vale da Pinta: the wilder, tougher sibling

Vale da Pinta plays 6,127 metres par 71, and it's widely considered the stronger test of the two Pestana courses. Ancient olive and carob trees survive as living obstacles throughout the layout, two lakes influence four holes, and strategic dog-legs punish an inaccurate drive more than Gramacho does. Bent-grass greens hold their pace year-round, which matters on a course where precision counts.

If you want a fun, varied resort round with a genuine design novelty and a tournament pedigree, play Gramacho. If you want the tougher, more characterful test — tighter driving, ancient trees in play, a course regulars rate as the better of the two — play Vale da Pinta. Green fees start from the same **€95** at both, and since they share a resort, playing both on the same trip is the obvious move.

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=gramacho,vale-da-pinta) to see Gramacho and Vale da Pinta's price, par, handicap limits and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

silves-vs-pestana-ferragudo-the-establis.text: Both courses belong to the Pestana group and sit inland from the coast, but that's about where the similarity ends. Silves has been open since 2006 and has a settled reputation for excellent conditioning. Pestana Ferragudo, on the other hand, only opened its doors on **1 September 2026** — so this comparison is really the old guard against the newest course in the Algarve.

Silves was designed by **Fausto Nascimento and Peter Booth** and opened in 2006 near the ancient Moorish town it's named after. Pestana Ferragudo, designed in-house by Pestana, is only a few weeks old at the time of writing — a genuinely new addition to the region's golf map, part of a wider residential development in Ferragudo village across the river from Portimão.
Silves: a known quantity, praised for its conditioning

Silves plays 5,615 metres par 70 over gently hilly terrain, with panoramic views over orange and olive groves and a layout that rewards accuracy more than power — a standout run of par-3s and four memorable par-5s. It's consistently well-regarded for how well it's maintained, which matters when so many Algarve courses struggle with conditioning in the peak summer months.
Pestana Ferragudo: too new to have a track record

Ferragudo plays 5,841 metres par 72 — longer than Silves — through parkland terrain that makes full use of the natural landscape. Having only opened this month, there's no track record yet on conditioning, pace of play or how it holds up once summer traffic properly arrives. If you're an early adopter who likes trying a course before the reviews pile up, this is your chance; if you'd rather wait for it to bed in, that's a reasonable call too.

If you want a reliable, well-conditioned round with an established reputation, play Silves — green fees start from **€95**. If you're curious about the newest course in the Algarve and don't mind being one of its first few thousand rounds, Ferragudo is worth the detour, with green fees from **€130** on Pestana's price list.

Want the numbers side by side instead? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=silves,pestana-ferragudo) to see Silves and Pestana Ferragudo's par, length and facilities pulled straight from our live course data.

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo) is the newest course in the Algarve and the new flagship of the Pestana group: an 18-hole, par-73 parkland layout that opened in 2026 between the fishing village of Ferragudo and Carvoeiro. It sits right next to Pestana's two older courses, [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) and [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta), which makes this corner of the western Algarve a very good base for a golf trip.

This guide answers one question: **where should you stay to play Ferragudo Golf Course?** Below are 11 hotels, resorts and villas within roughly 25 minutes of the first tee, starting with Pestana's own golf apartments next door, followed by places rated above 8 out of 10 by guests, from good-value rooms at around €50 a night to some of the best resorts in Portugal.
Is there a hotel at Ferragudo Golf Course?

Not yet. The course is part of Pestana Ferragudo Village, a new golf and residential development, and Pestana lists a boutique hotel among its planned facilities, but there is no opening date or booking page for it so far. For now, every golfer playing Ferragudo stays somewhere nearby and drives to the course.

The closest thing to an on-site hotel is Pestana Gramacho Residences, Pestana's own golf apartments on the neighbouring Gramacho course, about 12 minutes from Ferragudo by road. It is first on our list below. The closest well-rated hotel is actually Água Hotels Riverside, about 6 minutes away on the Ferragudo side of the Arade river.

The black pin is the course (tap it to see course details). The blue pins are the hotels in this guide; tap one to check prices and availability.
How we chose these hotels

Apart from Pestana Gramacho Residences, which we include because it is part of the same golf resort, every hotel on this list has a guest rating of at least 8 out of 10 on Booking.com and is no more than about 25 minutes from the course by car. Drive times are calculated by road, not in a straight line. We checked breakfast hours and golf services on each hotel's own website wherever possible, and we only mention a golf perk if the hotel or its operator actually states it.

Prices are the lowest nightly rates we found in October 2026 for the cheapest room or apartment, usually in the quieter months of November to February. Spring and autumn, which are peak golf season, cost more, so treat them as a guide rather than a quote.

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Pestana Gramacho Residences
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: Pestana's golf apartments sit right on the [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) course, part of the same Pestana golf resort as Ferragudo, and Pestana describes the property as "the perfect place for golf lovers". You get a golf academy on the doorstep, breakfast from 7am, a free internal shuttle and apartments with kitchens, about 12 minutes from Ferragudo and 6 minutes from Vale da Pinta. Its guest score of **7.8 on Booking.com** is a little lower than the rest of this list, but no other option puts you on a Pestana course with a golf academy on the doorstep.
Best value hotels near Ferragudo Golf Course (under €70 a night)

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Água Hotels Riverside
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: On the Ferragudo side of the Arade river, this is both the **closest well-rated hotel to the course**, about 6 minutes away, and the cheapest. It serves **breakfast from 7am**, which suits early tee times. There is a spa with sauna and jacuzzi, a gym that opens at 6am and free parking. Some guests find the décor a little dated, but for a golf trip on a budget it is hard to beat.

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Pestana Palm Gardens
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: Clifftop studios and apartments in Carvoeiro run by Pestana, the same group that owns Ferragudo. Pestana says guests get **exclusive benefits and discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta**, so it is a smart base if you want to play all three Pestana courses. Breakfast starts at 8am and is charged separately, but every unit has a kitchen, so an early bite before your round is easy.
perks: Discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Jupiter Marina Hotel
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: A stylish hotel on Portimão marina aimed at couples, with a spa, a rooftop bar and a free shuttle to Praia da Rocha beach. It scores **9.0 on Booking.com**, unusually high for the price, and breakfast starts at 7.30am. A good pick for golfing couples who want restaurants and nightlife within walking distance after the round. Parking is paid.
Mid-range hotels and villas near the course (€70 to €130 a night)

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Vale d'Oliveiras Quinta Resort & Spa
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: A five-star spa resort about 11 minutes from Ferragudo and only about 400 metres from Gramacho, according to the resort, with an à la carte restaurant, 24-hour room service and breakfast from 7.30am. It is popular with families, so it also works if you are travelling with non-golfers.

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Vale da Lapa Village Resort
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: Five-star villas set in gardens a few minutes from the course, with a spa, indoor pool and restaurant. At **9.3 on Booking.com** it is the best-rated resort this close to Ferragudo. The villas suit a group of friends who want their own space, and some have private pools for the end of the day.

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Quinta do Algarvio Village
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: Self-catering apartments with full kitchens and a saltwater pool that is heated in winter, around 12 minutes from the first tee. Guests rate it a remarkable **9.4 on Booking.com**. Members of the operator's Carvoeiro Clube Group club get discounts on golf within the group. There is no breakfast service, so plan to stock the fridge. You will need a car.

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Vale de Milho Village
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: Two- and three-bedroom townhouses, **each with its own private pool**, next to the [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) par-3 course, where guests get 20% off green fees. Prices are for the whole townhouse, so split between four golfers it is excellent value. It is a good choice for groups who want a short-game warm-up on the doorstep before heading to Ferragudo.
perks: 20% off green fees at Vale de Milho

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: Luxury hotels and golf resorts within 25 minutes

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Penina Hotel & Golf Resort
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: The Algarve's original golf resort, with three courses on site including the Sir Henry Cotton-designed [Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship). Penina's "Best Available Rate for Golfers" includes **a complimentary round every day** on one of its courses (a handicap certificate is needed for the Championship course). Combine a few rounds there with a day at Ferragudo, 15 minutes away. Breakfast starts at 7am.
perks: Free daily round on the golfer rate

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Tivoli Carvoeiro Algarve Resort
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: A five-star clifftop resort a short walk from Carvoeiro village, with sea views, a full spa and indoor and outdoor pools. It is one of the most established golf-holiday hotels in this area: UK golf tour operators sell packages here that include rounds at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta, and Ferragudo is about 23 minutes away.

hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.name: Vila Vita Parc
hotels-near-ferragudo-golf-course.text: One of the finest resorts in Portugal, on the clifftops at Porches. For golfers it has a driving range, a golf simulator, a 9-hole pitch and putt, an 18-hole putting green and a resident pro, and the resort says it offers **preferential rates and tee times at most Algarve courses**. Ideal if you are travelling with a non-golfing partner who wants a world-class spa and beach.
Ferragudo Golf Course green fees by season

According to Pestana's current price list, a round at Ferragudo costs around **€130 in low season** (December, January and June to August), **€200 in high season** (November, February, May and September) and **€230 in premium season** (March, April and October). Twilight rounds from 13:30 cost €80, which is a great option if your hotel is close by. Prices change, so confirm with the club before you book.
Tips for golfers staying near Ferragudo

**Hire a car.** None of the hotels above confirms a golf shuttle to Ferragudo, and the course is around 50 minutes to an hour from Faro Airport. Having your own car also makes it easy to add nearby courses such as [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta), [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) and [Morgado Golf](/courses/morgado), all within a short drive.

**Check breakfast times before you book.** If you like an early tee time, Pestana Gramacho Residences, Água Hotels Riverside and Penina all serve breakfast from 7am. Self-catering apartments and villas are the other way to get out early.

**Play all three Pestana courses.** Ferragudo, Gramacho and Vale da Pinta are all within about 12 minutes of each other. Pestana Gramacho Residences puts you right between them, and Pestana Palm Gardens guests get discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta.

Not sure Ferragudo is the right course for you? Read our comparison [Silves vs Pestana Ferragudo](/guide/silves-vs-pestana-ferragudo-the-established-course-and-the-brand-new-one), or browse every course in the area on the [Algarve golf map](/).
Frequently asked questions
Which hotel is closest to Ferragudo Golf Course?

Água Hotels Riverside, on the Ferragudo side of the Arade river, is the closest at around 6 minutes by car. Vale d'Oliveiras Quinta Resort & Spa and Vale da Lapa Village Resort are both about 11 minutes away, and Pestana's own Gramacho Residences and the Jupiter Marina Hotel about 12.
Is there a cheap hotel near Ferragudo Golf Course?
Yes. Água Hotels Riverside, 6 minutes from the course, has rooms from about €49 a night outside the summer months, and Pestana Palm Gardens has apartments from about €51.
Where should a group of golfers stay near Ferragudo?

For groups, villas and townhouses usually work out cheapest per person. Vale de Milho Village (private pool with every townhouse) and Vale da Lapa Village Resort (five-star villas) are both within about 20 minutes of the course.
Playing several courses? Find the best base for your trip

If Ferragudo is just one stop on your golf trip, try **Find Your Base** on the [Algarve Golf Map](/). Pick the courses you want to play and it shows you the area that sits closest to all of them, along with well-rated hotels nearby, so you spend less time driving and more time on the course.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

vila-sol-vs-vilamoura-old-course-which-s.text: If you are staying in Vilamoura and want one standout round, the choice often comes down to the **Old Course** and **Vila Sol**. They are only about seven minutes apart by car, both are long-established courses that have hosted the Portuguese Open, and both ask for a handicap of 28 for men and 36 for ladies. The big differences are price, layout and where you sleep.

The [Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course) was designed by Frank Pennink and opened in 1969, which makes it one of the oldest courses in the Algarve. It plays through mature umbrella pines at **par 73 and 6,254 metres** from the white tees (5,913 m from the yellows). In 2025 it was named **Portugal's Best Golf Course** at the World Golf Awards.

Today it is part of Vilamoura Golf, alongside Pinhal, Laguna and Millennium. Its clubhouse reopened in December 2024 after a refurbishment. You need a valid handicap certificate (maximum 28 for men and 36 for ladies), and only the club's own buggies are allowed. Green fees on the club's online booking run from about **€215 to €301** ([current Old Course green fees](/courses/vilamoura-old-course/green-fees)).
Vila Sol: 27 holes and a hotel on the course

[Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol) was designed by Donald Steel and opened in 1991. It hosted the Portuguese Open in 1992 and 1993. It has **27 holes in three nines, Prime, Challenge and Prestige**, each par 36, so any 18-hole round is par 72. From the white tees the combinations measure **6,274 to 6,393 metres**, with slope ratings of 135 to 137 from the white tees on the Portuguese Golf Federation's current table. That makes it a proper test, not an easy alternative.

Pestana runs the course and the five-star [Pestana Vila Sol Golf - Vilamoura](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/pestana-vila-sol-golf-and-conference.html) hotel right next to it, which scores 8.3 on Booking.com. The official 2026 rates are **€140** in December, January and June to August, €195 in most spring and autumn months and €215 at peak. A twilight round costs €60 ([current Vila Sol green fees](/courses/vila-sol/green-fees)). The handicap limit on the official scorecard is 28 for men and 36 for ladies.

In every season the Old Course costs more than Vila Sol, often by €80 or more for a single round. You are paying for the history, the setting and the 2025 award. If you plan to play several rounds, Vila Sol's twilight rate and its three nines make it the better value option.

**Play the Old Course** if this is your one big round in Vilamoura and you want a classic: a 1969 parkland course under the pines, with five decades of reputation behind it. **Play Vila Sol** if you would rather keep the budget for a second round, want a hotel on the course, or are staying several days and fancy trying different nine-hole combinations. Since they are so close, plenty of golfers play both.

The Pestana Vila Sol hotel is the only one of the two with a hotel on the course. The Old Course has no hotel of its own, but the hotels around Vilamoura marina are around 10 minutes away by car. See our guide to [golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura) for options at every price.
Both courses are around 25 to 30 km from Faro Airport by road, and a [pre-booked transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) gets you there with your clubs without hiring a car.

Want the numbers side by side? [Open the course comparator](/?compare=vila-sol,vilamoura-old-course) to compare price, handicap limits and facilities, or see every course in the area on our [Vilamoura golf courses page](/vilamoura/golf-courses).

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to Vilamoura costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-vilamoura-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-bette.text: Most golfers flying into Faro head for the middle of the Algarve: the Golden Triangle around [Quinta do Lago](/golf-resorts/quinta-do-lago) and [Vale do Lobo](/golf-resorts/vale-do-lobo), plus Vilamoura. That central stretch holds 22 of the region's 38 courses, and 12 of them start from €100 or more. On either side of it, the **western and eastern Algarve** offer two quite different golf holidays, and this guide compares them on the things that decide a trip: the courses, the green fees, the drive from the airport and where to stay.
West vs East Algarve at a glance

**Courses:** the west has 10 courses, nine full-length layouts plus Penina's 9-hole Resort Course, spread between Ferragudo and Vila do Bispo. The east has six full-length courses, all around Tavira and Castro Marim.
**Green fees:** five of the nine western full-length courses start below €80 for visitors. In the east, five of the six start at €100 or less, with Monte Rei the exception from €190.

**From Faro Airport:** the east is the closer side. Monte Rei quotes about 40 minutes by car and the other eastern courses are a similar drive. In the west, Penina quotes about 45 minutes, the Lagos courses are nearer an hour and Santo António, out towards Sagres, is the furthest of all.
**Golf resorts:** both sides have hotels built on a golf estate, four in the west and three in the east, covered further down.
Golf in the western Algarve: more courses, lower green fees

Around Portimão sits the most history. [Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship), designed by Sir Henry Cotton in 1966, was the first golf course built in the Algarve and starts from €77, while its 9-hole [Penina Resort](/courses/penina-resort) course costs from €28. In the hills behind, [Morgado](/courses/morgado) and [Alamos](/courses/alamos) sit side by side and start from €82 each (we compare them in [Alamos vs Morgado](/guide/alamos-vs-morgado-which-portimao-golf-course-should-you-play)). [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf), Sir Henry Cotton's 1991 design in Alvor, is the cheapest 18-hole round in the area from €75, and the brand-new [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo) opened in 2026 from €130.

Further west, around Lagos, the views take over. [Palmares](/courses/palmares) spreads 27 holes of clifftop and lakeside golf above Meia Praia beach, redesigned by Robert Trent Jones Jr., from €138. [Boavista](/courses/boavista) climbs the hillside above Lagos with sea views from €74, and [Espiche](/courses/espiche), opened in 2012, starts from €65 (see [Boavista vs Espiche](/guide/boavista-vs-espiche-which-lagos-golf-course-should-you-play)). Out on its own near Vila do Bispo, Pepe Gancedo's [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) is the most remote course in the region, from €57.
Golf in the eastern Algarve: Monte Rei and a compact cluster

The east is smaller but has the headline act. [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei), Jack Nicklaus's 2007 design near Vila Nova de Cacela, was ranked Portugal's number one course for 15 years in a row and remains a fixture in European top-10 lists. It is also the most expensive round on either side, from €190.

The rest of the east is far kinder on the wallet. [Quinta da Ria](/courses/quinta-da-ria) and [Quinta de Cima](/courses/quinta-de-cima) give you 36 holes by Rocky Roquemore on one estate beside the Ria Formosa natural park, both from €100 (compared in [Quinta da Ria vs Quinta de Cima](/guide/quinta-da-ria-vs-quinta-de-cima-which-tavira-course-should-you-play)). [Benamor](/courses/benamor), near Tavira, starts from €66. Close to the Spanish border, [Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim) starts from €87 and Seve Ballesteros's [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale) from €67 (see [Castro Marim vs Quinta do Vale](/guide/castro-marim-vs-quinta-do-vale-which-east-algarve-course-should-you-play)).
Handicap limits around the Algarve

Most courses on both sides use the standard Algarve limit of **28 for men and 36 for ladies**. In the west, Boavista is slightly stricter at 26 and 34, while Alto Golf accepts up to 36 for men and ladies. In the east, Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima also allow 36 for both, Monte Rei, Benamor and Quinta do Vale use 28 and 36, and Castro Marim asks for a handicap certificate without publishing a maximum.

If you play off a high handicap, check the limit before you book, or read [do you need a handicap to play golf in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) for the full rules and the courses that don't ask for one.
Where to stay on each side

**In the west**, [Penina Hotel & Golf Resort](/golf-resorts/penina) is a five-star hotel built around its two courses, from about €200 a night. [NAU Morgado Golf & Country Club](/golf-resorts/nau-morgado) sits between Morgado and Alamos, [Palmares Beach House](/golf-resorts/palmares) is a boutique five-star overlooking the Palmares course and Meia Praia, and [Boavista Golf & Spa Resort](/golf-resorts/boavista-golf-spa-resort) has townhouses and apartments beside its course. For hotels off the estates, see [hotels near Penina](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort) and [hotels near Morgado and Alamos](/guide/hotels-near-morgado-and-alamos-golf).

**In the east**, [Monte Rei](/golf-resorts/monte-rei) offers villas and apartments on its private estate, from about €390 a night. [Robinson Club Quinta da Ria](/golf-resorts/robinson-quinta-da-ria) is an all-inclusive resort between its two courses, and [Castro Marim](/golf-resorts/castro-marim-golf-resort) has village houses beside its course, from about €95 a night. More options are in [hotels near Monte Rei](/guide/hotels-near-monte-rei-golf).
So which side should you choose?

**Choose the west** if you want the most courses within reach of one base, lower green fees for most rounds, the history of Penina or the sea views at Palmares and Boavista. It suits longer trips, where playing somewhere different each day matters.
**Choose the east** if you want a shorter transfer from Faro, a round at Monte Rei, 36 holes from a single base at Quinta da Ria, or an all-inclusive stay at the Robinson Club.

The two ends of the region are well over an hour apart by car, so most golfers pick one side rather than splitting the week. If you would rather have everything within half an hour, compare the central [golf resorts](/golf-resorts) or browse every course on the [Algarve golf map](/). Green fees above are the lowest published visitor rates for the 2026/27 season; each course's page has the full price list by month.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve.text: Golf in the Algarve doesn't have to mean paying €200 a round. The most famous courses, such as the Vilamoura Old Course, Monte Rei and Quinta do Lago South, start at €188 to €215 for a single round. But plenty of full 18-hole courses cost a third of that. Here are the **cheapest golf courses in the Algarve**, ranked on their real green fees.
How we ranked them

Each price is the **lowest standard green fee a visitor can book for one round on their own**: no member, resident, junior or multi-round rates, and no packages that bundle a buggy. We took prices from each club's official price list or its own online booking for the 2026/27 season, checked in October 2026. Twilight rates are listed separately below. Prices change with the season, and most clubs that sell online adjust them day by day, so treat each figure as a starting point. Every course links to its own green fees page with the month-by-month prices. This ranking only covers courses whose prices we could check, so another course may be cheaper on a given day.
The 10 cheapest 18-hole golf courses in the Algarve
1. Santo António, Vila do Bispo: from €57

[Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) is the cheapest 18-hole course in the Algarve and also the westernmost, in the hills behind the fishing village of Salema. Its official 2026 rates are **€57** for most of the year and €68 from March to May and in September and October, with twilight rounds from 1:30pm for €35. It is par 71 and 5,712 metres, designed by Pepe Gancedo, and hilly enough that the club recommends a buggy. The club doesn't publish a handicap limit, so check when you book. [Santo António green fees](/courses/santo-antonio/green-fees)
2. Espiche, Lagos: from €65

[Espiche](/courses/espiche), west of Lagos, was designed by Peter Sauerman and opened in 2012. It plays 5,890 metres, par 72, through native scrub with views to the Monchique hills. On the club's own online booking it cost **€65** in December and €68 for most of the low and shoulder months, rising to €99 in spring. Summer twilight rounds were €54. [Espiche green fees](/courses/espiche/green-fees)
3. Benamor, Tavira: from €66

[Benamor](/courses/benamor), just outside Tavira, was laid out from Sir Henry Cotton's plans and opened in 2000. At 5,456 metres, par 71, it is one of the shortest 18-hole courses in the region. Its internet rates are **€66** in low season (December, January and June to August), €95 in mid-season and €103 in high season, with afternoon tee times in low season for €59. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Benamor green fees](/courses/benamor/green-fees)
4. Quinta do Vale, Castro Marim: from €67

[Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale), near the Spanish border, is a Seve Ballesteros design that opened in 2007. It plays 6,206 metres, par 72, with views over the Guadiana River. On the club's online booking it was **€67** in December and €68 in January and from June to August, rising to €99 in spring. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Quinta do Vale green fees](/courses/quinta-do-vale/green-fees)
5. Boavista, Lagos: from €74

[Boavista](/courses/boavista), on the edge of Lagos, is a hillside Howard Swan design from 2002 with views over the Bay of Lagos. Its online rate starts at about **€74** in low season, and its published rates for November 2026 to December 2027 run from €86 to €126. It has the strictest handicap rule on this list: 26 for men and 34 for ladies. [Boavista green fees](/courses/boavista/green-fees)
6. Alto Golf, Alvor: from €75

[Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) in Alvor, which Pestana describes as the last course Sir Henry Cotton designed, costs **€75** in December, January and June to August, €115 in November, February, May and September, and €140 in March, April and October. Twilight rounds from 3pm are only €50. It is par 70 and 5,432 metres, and it accepts handicaps up to 36 for men and ladies, which makes it one of the easiest full courses to get onto. [Alto Golf green fees](/courses/alto-golf/green-fees)
7. Penina Championship, Portimão: from about €77

[Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship), Sir Henry Cotton's 1966 course and the first 18-hole course built in the Algarve, is a surprise at this end of the list. Penina hasn't published a visitor price list since 2024/25, so our figure comes from booking agents: from about **€77** when we checked in September 2026. Its last official list started at €85 online. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Penina green fees](/courses/penina-championship/green-fees)
8. Salgados, Albufeira: from €78

[Salgados](/courses/salgados), on flat coastal land behind Praia da Galé, has water in play on almost every hole and the Salgados Lagoon nature reserve next door. On the club's online booking it cost **€78** in January, July and August and up to €139 in spring and autumn. Twilight rounds started at €47 in those cheaper months. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. [Salgados green fees](/courses/salgados/green-fees)
9. Morgado and Alamos, Portimão: from €82

The twin NAU courses north of Portimão share a clubhouse, a practice ground and a price list. [Morgado](/courses/morgado) is the longer and more open of the two at 6,581 metres, par 73; [Alamos](/courses/alamos) is shorter and tighter at 5,710 metres, par 71. Both cost **€82** in January and December (and in high summer) on the club's online booking, rising to €128 in spring. The handicap limit is 28 for men and 36 for ladies. Read [Alamos vs Morgado](/guide/alamos-vs-morgado-which-portimao-golf-course-should-you-play) to choose between them.
10. Castro Marim: from €80 to €87

[Castro Marim](/courses/castro-marim) has 27 holes in three nines near the Spanish border. Its official 2026 price list starts at **€80** for 18 holes in low season, while its online booking was showing €87 when we checked. The club asks for a handicap certificate but doesn't publish a maximum. [Castro Marim green fees](/courses/castro-marim/green-fees)

Just outside the top 10, [Vilamoura Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) start at **€88** in late autumn and winter, the cheapest way to play in Vilamoura. [Ombria](/courses/ombria), near Loulé, dropped to €85 in June but costs €99 to €216 the rest of the year.
The cheapest nine-hole rounds
If you only want a short round, or you are a beginner, nine holes cost far less:

**[Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho), Carvoeiro: €22.** A nine-hole, all par-3 course, 926 metres in total, with the same price all year. No handicap is needed, but the club expects you to have had a few lessons.

**[Penina Resort Course](/courses/penina-resort), Portimão: about €28.** A proper nine-hole par 35 by Sir Henry Cotton, with no handicap required. As with the Championship Course, Penina publishes no current rates, so this is the booking agents' price.
**[Balaia](/courses/balaia), Albufeira: €50 day fee.** A nine-hole par-3 course at Balaia Golf Village. The resort says a handicap is required but gives no limit.

**[Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs), Albufeira: €57 to €76.** Nine clifftop holes above the beach, including the famous par-3 Devil's Parlour. Players without a handicap are welcome from the red tees. For more short courses, see [the Algarve's best par-3 golf courses](/guide/the-algarve-s-best-par-3-golf-courses).
The cheapest twilight golf

Twilight rates for late-afternoon tee times can cut the price of a full course by a third or more. The cheapest we found on 18-hole courses were **€35 at Santo António** (from 1:30pm), **€47 at Salgados**, **€50 at Alto Golf** (from 3pm), **€54 at Espiche** in summer and **€55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves)**. Pestana's [Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol) and the new [Pestana Ferragudo](/courses/pestana-ferragudo), which start at €140 and €130 for a standard round, offer twilight for €60 and €80. Our [twilight golf guide](/guide/twilight-golf-in-the-algarve) has the start times and how much daylight you get each month. Just check the sunset time: in midwinter a late tee time may not leave enough light for 18 holes.
How to pay less at any Algarve course

**Pick your months.** At most courses on this list, the cheapest months are December, January and June to August. Spring (March to May) and October are the most expensive, because that is when most golfers visit. Our guide to the [Algarve golf season](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf) explains the trade-offs month by month.
**Book on the club's own website.** Many clubs sell their lowest online rates directly. Boavista's web rate, for example, is lower than its published rack rate.

**Look west or east.** The cheapest courses are at the two ends of the Algarve: around Lagos, Portimão and Vila do Bispo in the west, and Tavira and Castro Marim in the east. The Golden Triangle and Vilamoura's best-known courses are the most expensive. Our guide to [west vs east Algarve](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf) compares the two sides, and each town page, from [Lagos](/lagos/golf-courses) to [Tavira](/tavira/golf-courses), puts every local green fee in one table.

**Check your handicap first.** A cheap round is no use if you can't get on. Most of these courses ask for 28 for men and 36 for ladies; Alto Golf accepts 36 for everyone, and Boavista is stricter at 26 and 34. Our guide to [handicap rules in the Algarve](/guide/do-you-need-a-handicap-to-play-golf-in-the-algarve) has the details.
Want to compare prices yourself? Open the [Algarve golf course map](/) to see every course's green fees, handicap limits and facilities side by side.

**How much will the trip cost?** See our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) if you book it yourself, with month-by-month totals and example hotels.

**Booking your rounds?** Our guide to [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve) shows how each course takes bookings, when to book and the cancellation rules to check.

**Playing several times a week?** Our guide to [long-stay golf in the Algarve](/guide/long-stay-golf-in-the-algarve) explains when a short-term membership or a round package works out cheaper than paying per round.

alto-golf-vs-penina-championship-which-p.text: Between Portimão and Alvor, 15 minutes apart, sit two courses linked to the same man: Sir Henry Cotton, three-time Open champion. **Penina** was the first 18-hole course built in the Algarve, in 1966. **Alto Golf**, opened in 1991, is described by its operator Pestana as the last course Cotton designed. Their names may be linked, but they play very differently.
Penina Championship: where Algarve golf began

Penina's [Sir Henry Cotton Championship Course](/courses/penina-championship) was built on former rice paddy fields, which explains its streams and water hazards on flat ground. It is a long course: **par 73 and 6,273 metres** from the white tees. The back nine alone is par 38, because four of its five par 5s come in pairs. With official slope ratings of 143 from the whites and 138 from the yellows, it is one of the more demanding courses in the western Algarve.

The club says the course has hosted the Portuguese Open ten times. Its signature hole is the par-3 13th, with a lake on the right, which the club notes was voted one of the best 500 holes in the world. You need a handicap certificate, with a maximum of 28 for men and 36 for ladies.

Penina has not published a visitor price list since 2024/25, when its online rates ran from €85 to €121. Check our [Penina green fees page](/courses/penina-championship/green-fees) for current prices before you book.
Alto Golf: shorter, cheaper, more welcoming

[Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) in Alvor was inaugurated in 1991. Today it is a much shorter course than Penina: the current official scorecard shows **par 70 and 5,432 metres** from the white tees. Its 16th hole was once famous as a 600-metre-plus par 5, one of the longest holes in Europe. It has since been shortened, and the longest hole is now the par-5 18th at 506 metres.
Alto is also the more welcoming of the two for higher handicappers: its official scorecard sets a **handicap limit of 36 for both men and ladies**. It has a driving range and golf academy.

Pestana's published prices are **€75** in December, January and June to August, €115 in November, February, May and September, and €140 in March, April and October. Twilight rounds from 3pm are €50 ([current Alto Golf green fees](/courses/alto-golf/green-fees)).

**Play Penina** for the history and the challenge. It is a long, flat championship course where the Algarve's golf story began. It suits lower handicappers who want a proper test. **Play Alto Golf** if you want a more relaxed, shorter round at a lower price, if your handicap is above 28, or if you are fitting golf around a beach holiday in Alvor. Being so close, they also make an easy pair for two days' golf.

Penina has its own five-star hotel, the [Penina Hotel & Golf Resort](https://www.booking.com/hotel/pt/penina-hotel-golf-resort.html), which scores 8.5 on Booking.com. Hotel guests pay reduced green fees, and the "Best Available Rate for Golfers" room offer includes a free round every day. Alto Golf has no hotel of its own, but Alvor's beach hotels are only a few minutes away. Our guide to [hotels near Penina Golf Resort](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort) covers both.
Both courses are about 75 to 80 km from Faro Airport by road. A [pre-booked transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) is the easiest way to get there with your clubs if you are not hiring a car.

Want the numbers side by side? **You will need a car.** Silves is inland, a little over 60 km from Faro Airport. A [hire car](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw) is the practical option, or book a [private transfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA) to your hotel.
**More golf nearby.** Amendoeira is about 17 minutes away and Pestana's Gramacho, at Carvoeiro, about 19. See our [Silves golf courses page](/silves/golf-courses).

hotels-near-pestana-carvoeiro-golf.text: Pestana Carvoeiro is a two-course golf resort in the countryside just north of Carvoeiro. The two clubhouses are only about a kilometre apart.

This guide covers the best hotels near Pestana Carvoeiro golf: Pestana's own golf apartments on the Gramacho course, four excellent resorts within about five minutes, and good-value and clifftop options in and around Carvoeiro, all within 15 minutes.

Tips for golfers staying near Pestana Carvoeiro

**Play both courses.** They are very different, and the green fees are the same. Not sure where to start? Read [Gramacho vs Vale da Pinta](/guide/gramacho-vs-vale-da-pinta-which-pestana-carvoeiro-course-should-you-play).

**Getting there.** Faro Airport is about an hour's drive east, and Portimão is 15 minutes west if you want a bigger town for an evening out.

best-value-golf-in-the-algarve.text: The cheapest green fee isn't always the cheapest round. At some Algarve courses the price includes a buggy; at others you pay €40 to €55 on top. Add club hire, range balls and a trolley, and a course that looked expensive can work out cheaper than one that looked like a bargain. This guide to **best value golf in the Algarve** compares what you actually pay, not just the headline green fee.

We don't rank courses by quality, because that comes down to taste. Instead we look at what your money gets you: whether a buggy is included, which deals bundle one in, and the cheapest course of each type, from sea views to tournament history. Prices come from each club's official price list or its own online booking for the 2026/27 season, checked in October and November 2026. It isn't a complete list: we've only included courses where the club publishes enough information, so a course missing here may still be good value. Always confirm the price when you book.
The real price of a round with a buggy

This table adds the buggy to the lowest green fee for one player, at the courses that publish a buggy price or include one. The cheapest months differ from course to course, so the totals don't all apply at the same time of year.

best-value-golf-in-the-algarve.note: Most clubs don't say whether the buggy price is per buggy or per person. If it is per buggy and you share with a partner, your half costs less. Boavista's tariff doesn't say whether its €45 covers 18 or 9 holes. Sources: club price lists and online booking, October and November 2026.

best-value-golf-in-the-algarve.text: The surprise is how well the buggy-included courses come out. [Ombria](/courses/ombria) near Loulé dropped to €85 with a shared buggy in June, and still cost €99 to €101 in July, August, September and December. [Amendoeira](/courses/amendoeira-oconnor)'s online rate of €100 in December and January includes a buggy if one is available, which is less than one player pays for a green fee and buggy at Gramacho, Vale da Pinta or Silves in the same months.

If you're happy to walk, the order changes: Santo António, Benamor and Boavista are then the cheapest on this list. Our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) has the rules and the courses that don't publish a buggy price.
Pestana's two players and a buggy deal

Pestana's official price list has a summer special for two players sharing one buggy at its Algarve courses. In every case it costs less than two green fees plus a buggy, and at most courses less than two green fees on their own, so the buggy effectively comes free.

best-value-golf-in-the-algarve.text: To put that in context, two standard green fees at Gramacho cost €190 from June to August, before you add a €55 buggy. The special is €184 for both of you with the buggy. In the second half of May and in September, two green fees cost €310 against a special of €270. At Alto Golf in summer the special is €4 more than two green fees, but it includes the €55 buggy. If you're travelling as a pair and playing a Pestana course in summer, this is usually the rate to book.

Other clubs run similar bundles at different times of year, including Quinta do Vale, Quinta da Ria, Quinta de Cima and Quinta do Lago. The buggy guide lists the [current buggy offers](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve) with their dates.
The cheapest course of each type
Value depends on what you want from a round. Here's the lowest price we found for each kind of course, based on the same official prices.
Sea views: Boavista from €74

Of the 18-hole courses tagged **ocean view** on our map, [Boavista](/courses/boavista) above Lagos is the cheapest, from €74 in January, June, July, August and December. It's a hillside course, so think about a buggy. For the Algarve's most famous sea hole, the clifftop 16th on [Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal), green fees start at €116 in January, February, November and December. If nine holes are enough, [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho) costs €22 and [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) from €57. See [the best ocean view golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-best-ocean-view-golf-courses-in-the-algarve) for more.
A buggy in the price: Ombria from €85

[Ombria](/courses/ombria), [Amendoeira](/courses/amendoeira-faldo) and [Monte Rei](/courses/monte-rei) include a buggy in the green fee, and Ombria is the cheapest of the three. At [Vale do Lobo](/courses/vale-do-lobo-ocean), full-paying adults get a shared buggy with the Sunset rate, which costs €76 to €101 depending on the month.
A course you can walk: Salgados from €78

[Salgados](/courses/salgados) near Albufeira sits on flat land behind the beach, and Where2Golf says players generally walk it. It costs from €78 in January, July and August. [Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship) is similarly flat and costs about €77 through booking agents, though the club itself hasn't published current rates. [Vilamoura Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium), another flat course, is €88 in December. Our guide to [Algarve golf courses you can walk](/guide/algarve-golf-courses-you-can-walk) has the full picture.
Tournament history: Penina from about €77

[Penina Championship](/courses/penina-championship), Sir Henry Cotton's 1966 course and the first in the Algarve, says it has hosted the Portuguese Open ten times. At about €77 it's the cheapest way we found to play a course with tour history. [Vila Sol](/courses/vila-sol), which hosted the Portuguese Open in 1992 and 1993, costs from €140, or €104 each with Pestana's summer special for two. The [Vilamoura Old Course](/courses/vilamoura-old-course), which hosted the event in 1979, starts at €215 in December.

best-value-golf-in-the-algarve.text: Club hire is the extra that adds up fastest over a week. Over four rounds at a Pestana course, it comes to €180, which can be more than your airline charges to fly your own clubs. Compare the two with our [airline golf bag guides](/guide) and the [club rental options](/club-rental) before you decide. Getting to the course costs money too, and our guide to [Faro Airport to Algarve golf courses](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses) covers transfer and car hire costs.
Cheaper ways to play the same course

**Play late.** Twilight rates can cut a green fee by a third or more. Pestana's are €50 to €80, from 1:30pm at Ferragudo and 3pm or 3:30pm at its other courses, with a twilight buggy at €40. See our [twilight golf guide](/guide/twilight-golf-in-the-algarve), and Santo António's is €35 from 1:30pm. Our guide to [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve) lists more.

**Pick your months.** At most courses, December, January and June to August are cheapest, while March, April and October cost the most. The [Algarve golf season guide](/guide/algarve-golf-season-best-time-to-play-golf) explains the trade-offs.
**Book the bundle, not the parts.** If you want a buggy, look for a rate that includes one before adding it on arrival. The deals above are the clearest examples.
Frequently asked questions
Is golf expensive in the Algarve?

It depends on the course. The cheapest 18-hole rounds start at €57 to €67 in low season, while the best-known courses, such as Monte Rei, Quinta do Lago South and the Vilamoura Old Course, start at €188 to €215. Most courses fall between the two. Our guide to [how much a golf trip to the Algarve costs](/guide/how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve-cost) puts green fees together with flights, hotels and transport.
Which Algarve golf course is the best value?

There's no single answer, because it depends on what you want. If you need a buggy, Ombria and Amendoeira come out well because theirs is included. If you walk, Santo António, Benamor and Salgados are hard to beat. If you're a pair playing in summer, Pestana's two-player deal is one of the best rates we found.
Are buggies included in Algarve green fees?

Usually not. Of the courses we checked, Ombria, Monte Rei and Amendoeira include one, and Vale do Lobo includes a shared buggy with its Sunset rate. Elsewhere, buggy hire costs €40 to €55 where the club publishes a price.
Ready to compare? Open the [Algarve golf course map](/) to see every course's green fees, handicap limits and facilities side by side.

**Booking your rounds?** Our guide to [how to book tee times in the Algarve](/guide/how-to-book-tee-times-in-the-algarve) shows how each course takes bookings, when to book and the cancellation rules to check.

**Playing several times a week?** Our guide to [long-stay golf in the Algarve](/guide/long-stay-golf-in-the-algarve) explains when a short-term membership or a round package works out cheaper than paying per round.

how-much-does-a-golf-trip-to-the-algarve.text: Why the hotel cost is the least certain figure

Our hotel prices are the lowest "from" rates we found in autumn 2026, and we couldn't confirm rates for specific dates in January or April. That's why the totals say "from". Expect to pay more in busy periods, and check your exact dates before you rely on these figures.

Summer makes the biggest difference. According to Statistics Portugal (INE), the average rate for an occupied room in the Algarve was **€217.80 in August 2025**, the highest of any region in Portugal. In January 2026, the Algarve's average was below the national figure of €92.10. These are averages across all types of accommodation, not the prices of our example hotels, but they show why a summer trip will usually cost more than the totals above.
Food and drink: an estimate, not a price list

Travel budget guides commonly suggest about €40 to €60 per person a day for eating out in the Algarve, although none of them is an official survey. We used €40 a day for the value trip, €50 for the mid-range trip and €60 for the premium trip. A good dinner at a resort could easily cost more.
Getting around: hire car or transfers

We used a small hire car because the example courses are spread out. Kayak's average for a small car at Faro Airport is about €15 a day, or €75 for 5 days before fuel and tolls. Its averages across all car types range from about €9 a day in January to €25 in July, so treat these as a guide and [compare car hire for your dates](https://economybookings.tpo.li/Qf5waAWw).

If you're staying near your courses, you may not need a car. Pre-booked sedan transfers from Faro Airport were quoted at about €34 to Quinta do Lago, €35 to Vilamoura and €81 to Portimão in October 2026, per vehicle and each way. You can [compare transfers on GetTransfer](https://gettransfer.tpo.li/9bs77WsA). See our guides to [Faro Airport to Vilamoura](/guide/faro-airport-to-vilamoura-with-golf-clubs) and other Algarve areas for details.
Flights and your golf bag

We've left flights out of the totals because fares vary so much by date, airline and departure airport. Remember to add the cost of your golf bag, which varies by airline. We have guides for [Ryanair](/guide/ryanair-golf-clubs-what-it-costs-to-fly-with-your-own-set-to-the-algarve), [easyJet](/guide/golf-clubs-on-easyjet-rules-sizes-and-what-it-actually-costs) and [Jet2](/guide/jet2-golf-clubs-fees-weight-limits-and-why-you-shouldn-t-leave-booking-late).
Golf extras to budget for

These aren't in the totals, so add them if you need them. Buggy hire is €55 for 18 holes at Alto, €50 at Salgados and €45 at Boavista. Some courses don't publish a price, so see our [guide to golf buggy hire in the Algarve](/guide/golf-buggy-hire-in-the-algarve). Hiring a full set of clubs costs €45 at Pestana's courses, such as Alto, and €50 at Salgados.
How to spend less on your Algarve golf trip
**Compare months.** The same four rounds on our value trip cost €313 in January and €504 in April. Check the green fees page for each course, as the cheapest month varies.
**Look at twilight rates.** Alto, for example, lists a twilight rate of €50 from 15:00, against €75 to €140 for its standard round. Just make sure there's enough daylight to finish.

**Choose lower-priced courses.** Green fees vary widely, from €57 at [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) to over €300 at the most expensive times on some premium courses. See [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).

**Look for rates with a shared buggy.** If you want a buggy anyway, a combined rate can be simpler than adding one later. Santo António's 2026 list, for example, has one round for two players with a buggy at €124 to €147 in total.
Is a package cheaper than booking it yourself?

This guide doesn't answer that, because it only covers trips you book yourself. Package prices depend on the company, dates and what's included, so compare a real quote with your own total, using the same hotel, courses and dates.

**Only have a weekend?** Our [guide to a golf weekend in the Algarve](/guide/golf-weekend-in-the-algarve) costs a Friday-to-Monday trip with two rounds, from four bases within about 45 minutes of Faro Airport.

**Travelling as a group?** Our guide to [Algarve golf trips for groups and golf societies](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies) covers golf villas and apartments, booking tee times together, buggies and minivans.
