algarve-golf-in-january.text: Is January a good month for golf in the Algarve? It's one of the best-value months of the year. Afternoons average about **16°C**, frost is virtually unknown on the coast, and on 20 of the 30 courses we track January shares the lowest green fee of the year. The trade-offs are short days, with the sun setting between about 5.25pm and 5.55pm, and around six rainy days in the month.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in January from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay, and how busy it gets.
Algarve weather in January for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

algarve-golf-in-january.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of January, in Portuguese winter time (the same as UK time).
algarve-golf-in-january.caption: January weather in the Algarve

algarve-golf-in-january.text: January is the coolest month of the year, but only just: the average high is 16°C in both Faro and Sagres, and the average low is a little over 8°C. Rain falls on about six days in Faro and seven in Sagres, which leaves more than three weeks of dry golf, and only one or two days in the month see heavy rain. The days get longer through the month, with sunset about half an hour later by the end of January than at the start.
What January weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** After the wet weeks of late autumn and December, fairways can be soft in January and the ball won't run far, so courses play a little longer than their yardage suggests. Some clubs keep buggies on the paths after heavy rain. The upside is lush, green turf and greens that hold a well-struck approach.

**Tee times.** With under ten hours of daylight in early January, aim to tee off by about 1pm if you want to finish 18 holes in daylight, a little later by the end of the month. Late morning is the sweet spot: the frost-free mornings can still be chilly and dewy, and the warmest part of the day is early afternoon.

**What to pack.** Think layers: a base layer, a jumper or fleece and a waterproof jacket you can take off as the day warms up. Waterproof trousers, an umbrella and a spare glove are worth their space, and a beanie for the first few holes of an early round. On a clear day you'll still want sun cream.
Green fees in January

January is part of the Algarve's winter low season. On 20 of the 30 courses we track, January shares the lowest green fee of the year, and on average fees are about **33% below** each course's peak price. The big-name courses offer the largest savings in cash terms.

algarve-golf-in-january.note: The lowest price any visitor can book for one 18-hole round, from each club's official price list or its own online booking, checked in October 2026. All year shows the course's cheapest and dearest months. Prices change, so check before you book.
algarve-golf-in-january.caption: January green fees: 18 holes, visitor rate

algarve-golf-in-january.text: Twilight rounds are cheaper again: this January they start from €35 at Santo António, €47 at [Salgados](/courses/salgados) and €50 at Alto Golf, and Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho) and [Silves](/courses/silves) courses offer them at €55. With the light going by late afternoon, check the start time so you know how many holes you'll get in. For more ways to save, see [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in January

Temperatures are almost identical across the region in January, so pick your base for the courses you want to play rather than the weather. The west sees slightly more rainy days than the centre and east, but the difference is about one day a month. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).

Low-season prices make January a good time to tick off a premium course: Amendoeira's Faldo Course costs €100, less than half its spring price, and Quinta do Lago South €188 against €264 at peak. Short of time on a winter afternoon? A nine-hole course such as [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) or [Balaia](/courses/balaia) fits neatly into the daylight.
Crowds and what else is on in January

After the New Year week, January is one of the quietest months on the Algarve's fairways. Tee sheets are open, you can often book a day or two ahead, and rounds tend to flow at a good pace. The almond trees start to blossom in the Algarve countryside from late January, which brightens up the inland courses.
Prices for hotels are generally low, but some seasonal resort hotels close for part of the winter, so check your hotel is open on your dates before you book flights.
Frequently asked questions
Is January a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, if you want low prices and quiet courses. Afternoons average 16°C, frost is very rare on the coast, and green fees are at or near their lowest of the year on most courses. Expect short days and about six rainy days in the month.
Is the Algarve warm enough for golf in January?
Yes. The average daily high is about 16°C in both Faro and Sagres, and the average low around 8°C. Most golfers play in a long-sleeved top and a jumper, with a waterproof layer for showers.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in January?
Faro averages 49 mm of rain in January over about six rainy days, and Sagres 53 mm over about seven. Heavy rain, of 10 mm or more in a day, falls on only one or two days in the month.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in January?
The sun sets at about 5.25pm at the start of January and about 5.55pm by the end. To finish 18 holes in daylight, aim to tee off by around 1pm.

algarve-golf-in-february.text: Is February a good month for golf in the Algarve? For many golfers it's one of the best. Afternoons average about **17°C**, February is the driest month of the winter in Faro, with around five rainy days, and the days stretch out noticeably, with the sun setting after 6pm by the end of the month. The catch is that green fees start to rise as the spring golf season gets going.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in February from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and when it gets busy.
Algarve weather in February for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of February, in Portuguese winter time (the same as UK time).

algarve-golf-in-february.text: February is a touch warmer than January, with an average high of 17°C in Faro, and drier: about 42 mm of rain over five rainy days, the lowest of any winter month. Sagres is slightly cooler and wetter, with six rainy days. Daylight grows by almost an hour over the month, which makes a big difference to how late you can tee off.
What February weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** Courses are usually drying out from the winter rain by February, but fairways can still be soft after a wet spell, so don't expect summer roll. Greens are in good condition but not yet at their spring pace.
**Tee times.** To finish 18 holes in daylight, tee off by about 1.30pm in early February and by about 2pm at the end of the month. Mid-morning starts give you the best of the day's warmth.

**What to pack.** Layers still rule: a base layer, a light jumper and a waterproof jacket. You'll often shed the jumper by the back nine on a sunny afternoon. Bring waterproof trousers and an umbrella just in case, and sun cream, because the February sun has more strength than it feels.
Green fees in February

February is a transition month. Some courses keep their low-season prices, but many move into their spring rates: on average, February fees are about **15% below** each course's peak price, against about a third below in January. The jump can be steep at the resort courses, so if your dates are flexible, compare the price with late January before you book.

For more ways to save, see [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in February

The weather is very similar across the region in February: the west gets about one more rainy day a month and is slightly cooler, but not enough to plan around. Choose your base for the courses and prices you want. The western courses around Lagos and Sagres have the lowest green fees in our table this month, and Espiche and Santo António stay at or near their low-season prices. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Crowds and what else is on in February

Courses are generally quiet in the first half of February and get busier through the month. The UK's February half-term brings a busier week, usually in the middle of the month, when families and groups arrive, so book tee times ahead if you're travelling then.

The almond blossom is at its best in the Algarve countryside in February, and carnival comes to Portugal before Lent: Carnival Tuesday falls on 9 February in 2027, with parades in towns such as Loulé. It's a good time to visit as more seasonal hotels reopen ahead of spring, but check your hotel is open on your dates.
Frequently asked questions
Is February a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes. It's usually the driest month of the winter, afternoons average 17°C and the days are getting longer. Green fees rise during February on many courses, so it's not quite as cheap as January.
Is the Algarve hot in February?
No, it's mild rather than hot. The average high is 17°C in Faro and 16°C in Sagres, and the average low is about 9°C. That's comfortable golfing weather in a long-sleeved top.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in February?
Faro averages 42 mm of rain in February over about five rainy days, and Sagres 49 mm over about six. Days of heavy rain are rare, at one or two a month.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in February?
The sun sets at about 5.55pm at the start of February and about 6.25pm at the end. To finish 18 holes in daylight, tee off by about 1.30pm to 2pm.

algarve-golf-in-march.text: Is March a good month for golf in the Algarve? The weather says yes: afternoons average about **19°C**, there are around six rainy days, and after the clocks go forward at the end of the month it stays light until nearly 8pm. The catch is the price. March is peak season, and on 22 of the 30 courses we track it's already the most expensive month of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in March from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay, and how to plan around Easter.
Algarve weather in March for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

algarve-golf-in-march.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of March, in Portuguese local time; the clocks go forward an hour on the last Sunday of March, as in the UK.
algarve-golf-in-march.caption: March weather in the Algarve

algarve-golf-in-march.text: March is noticeably warmer than February, with an average high of almost 19°C in Faro and mornings around 11°C. It isn't the driest month, though: about 47 mm of rain falls over around six days, usually in short spells rather than long wet weeks. The biggest change is the light: the days lengthen by more than an hour over the month, and the clock change moves sunset from about 6.25pm to almost 7.55pm.
What March weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** With spring growth under way, the courses come into good shape in March: fairways firm up between showers, the grass thickens and greens pick up pace. After a wet day, expect a little less roll.

**Tee times.** Until the clocks change, tee off by about 2pm to finish 18 holes in daylight. After the change at the end of the month, you can start as late as about 3.30pm. Morning rounds can be fresh; by early afternoon it's usually short-sleeve weather in the sun.
**What to pack.** Short sleeves for the afternoons, a light jumper or windproof for the mornings, and a waterproof jacket for the showers. Sun cream and a cap become essential this month.
Green fees in March

March is when the Algarve's spring peak begins. On 22 of the 30 courses we track, March is already at the course's highest price of the year, and on average fees are only about **5% below** peak. The exceptions are worth knowing: Amendoeira's Faldo Course charges €138 in March against €212 in April and May, and [Salgados](/courses/salgados) €102 on its own booking site against €139 in April.

Where to play in March

The weather is very similar across the region in March, so choose your base for the courses and the price. The western courses in our table, such as Santo António, Espiche and [Boavista](/courses/boavista), are among the best value in peak season. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Easter, crowds and the clock change

March gets busier as it goes on. Spring golf packages fill the tee sheets, and Easter brings the busiest stretch of the spring: in 2027, Easter Sunday is on 28 March, so the UK Easter school holidays run from late March into April. Book tee times and hotels well ahead if you're travelling then, and expect popular courses to be fully booked at peak times.

The clocks go forward an hour on the last Sunday of March, the same day as in the UK, so there's no time difference to think about. Easter weekend in 2027 is also the weekend the clocks change, so double-check your tee time on 28 March.
Frequently asked questions
Is March a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, for the weather and the courses. Afternoons average 19°C, the courses are coming into their best condition and the days are long after the clocks change. It is peak season, though, so green fees are high and tee times book up, especially around Easter.
Is the Algarve warm in March?
Warm enough for golf in short sleeves on most afternoons. The average high is 19°C in Faro and 18°C in Sagres, with mornings around 11°C.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in March?
Faro averages 47 mm of rain in March over about six rainy days, and Sagres 49 mm over a similar number. The rain usually comes in short spells.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in March?
The sun sets at about 6.25pm at the start of March. After the clocks go forward on the last Sunday of the month, sunset moves to about 7.50pm.

algarve-golf-in-april.text: Is April a good month for golf in the Algarve? For conditions, it's one of the best months of the year: afternoons average about **21°C**, there are about five rainy days, the courses are in excellent shape and it stays light until after 8pm. It's also the most expensive month: on 28 of the 30 courses we track, April green fees are the highest of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in April from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and how to get the most from peak season.
Algarve weather in April for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

algarve-golf-in-april.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of April, in Portuguese summer time (the same as UK time).

algarve-golf-in-april.text: April brings the first properly warm afternoons of the year, with an average high of about 21°C in Faro, though mornings still start around 12°C. Rain falls on about five days in the month and heavy rain is rare. Sagres is about a degree and a half cooler in the afternoon, and the far west tends to feel fresher in the Atlantic breeze.
What April weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** April is when the Algarve's courses are usually at their best: the grass is growing strongly after the winter rain, fairways are firm and green, and greens are quick and true.

**Tee times.** With more than 13 hours of daylight and sunset after 7.50pm, you can tee off as late as about 3.30pm to 4pm and still finish 18 holes. That opens up an afternoon round after a morning at the beach, or two rounds in one day.
**What to pack.** Short sleeves and a light jumper or windproof for the mornings, plus a light waterproof just in case. The sun is strong by April, so pack sun cream, a cap and sunglasses.
Green fees in April

April is the peak of the Algarve's spring golf season. On 28 of the 30 courses we track, April fees are the highest of the year, so you'll pay full rate almost everywhere. That makes value courses and twilight rounds more important than in any other month.

Where to play in April

Because prices are at their peak almost everywhere, April is the month to think hardest about value. The cheapest 18-hole courses in our table are in the far west and east of the region, such as Santo António, Espiche, Quinta do Vale and Benamor, all around €100 or less.

If you're planning one premium round on your trip, it may be worth moving it to another month: Monte Rei costs €312 in April against €190 in December, and Amendoeira's Faldo Course €212 against €100. Easter, crowds and booking ahead

April is one of the busiest months of the year on the Algarve's courses. The Easter school holidays carry on into early April (Easter Sunday is on 28 March in 2027), and spring golf groups fill the tee sheets throughout the month. Book tee times as early as you can, especially for morning slots at the best-known courses, and book your hotel well ahead.
25 April is a national holiday in Portugal, Freedom Day, so expect some local demand for tee times around that date as well.
Frequently asked questions
Is April a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, it's one of the best months for conditions: warm afternoons, long days and courses in top shape. It's also the most expensive and one of the busiest months, so book early and look at twilight rates.
Is the Algarve hot in April?
Warm rather than hot. The average high is about 21°C in Faro and 19°C in Sagres, with mornings around 12°C.
Does it rain in the Algarve in April?
A little. Faro averages 39 mm of rain in April over about five rainy days, and Sagres 35 mm over about six. Heavy downpours are rare.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in April?
The sun sets at about 7.55pm at the start of April and about 8.20pm by the end. You can tee off as late as about 3.30pm to 4pm and still finish 18 holes.

algarve-golf-in-may.text: Is May a good month for golf in the Algarve? Many golfers think it's the best of all. Afternoons average about **23°C**, rain falls on only about four days, and by the end of the month it's light until about 8.45pm. As in April, you pay for it: on 18 of the 30 courses we track, May shares the highest green fee of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in May from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where to play.
Algarve weather in May for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

algarve-golf-in-may.text: May is warm, dry and long. The average high is 23.5°C in Faro and mornings start around 15°C. Faro has about nine or ten days of 25°C or more in an average May, but only about one above 30°C, so it rarely gets uncomfortably hot. **Fairways and greens.** Courses are usually in excellent condition in May: firm, fast fairways that give you plenty of roll, and quick greens. Bring your short game, because firm greens can be hard to hold.

**Tee times.** You have more than 14 hours of daylight, so you can tee off as late as about 4pm and still finish. Morning tee times are the most comfortable as the month warms up, and late afternoon rounds are a pleasure as the heat goes out of the day.

**What to pack.** Summer golf kit: short sleeves, shorts if the club's dress code allows them, a cap, sunglasses and plenty of sun cream. A light windproof for an early start, and a refillable water bottle.
Green fees in May

May stays in the Algarve's spring peak. On 18 of the 30 courses we track, May shares the highest price of the year, and on average fees are only about **5% below** peak. Some courses ease off slightly: Gramacho charges €155 in May against €180 in March and April.

Crowds and what else is on in May

The UK's late-May bank holiday and half-term week, at the end of the month, bring a busier spell, so book ahead if you're travelling then. 1 May is a public holiday in Portugal.
Hotels are busy but not yet at their summer peak, so you'll usually find more choice and lower room rates than in July and August.

Is May a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Warm, and occasionally hot. The average high is 23.5°C in Faro, with about one day above 30°C in an average May. The far west, around Sagres, is about two degrees cooler.

algarve-golf-in-june.text: Is June a good month for golf in the Algarve? Yes, if you tee off early. Afternoons average about **27°C**, it barely rains, and these are the longest days of the year, with sunrise around 6.15am and sunset around 8.50pm. And as the heat builds, green fees fall: on 11 of the 30 courses we track, June shares the lowest price of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in June from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off to beat the heat, what you'll pay and where to play.
Algarve weather in June for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

algarve-golf-in-june.text: June is the start of the Algarve summer. The average high in Faro is almost 27°C, with around five days above 30°C, while Sagres in the far west averages 24°C and has only about one. Rain is very rare: about 5 mm falls in the whole month, usually on a single day or none at all. With almost 15 hours of daylight, you can plan your golf around the cooler hours.
What June weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** Courses are well irrigated through the summer, so they stay green, but the fairways run firm and fast in June. You'll get plenty of roll off the tee, and you'll need to land approach shots short of the flag.

**Tee times.** The best time to play in June is early: tee off between 7am and 9am and you'll finish before the hottest part of the day. Late afternoon is the other comfortable window: with sunset around 8.50pm, a 4.30pm start still gets you round before dark.
**What to pack.** Light, breathable golf clothes, a hat, sunglasses and high-factor sun cream. Carry more water than you think you'll need, and consider taking a buggy for a midday round.
Green fees in June

June is when green fees start to drop into the summer low season. On 11 of the 30 courses we track, June shares the lowest price of the year, and on average fees are about **28% below** each course's peak. Amendoeira's Faldo Course falls to €109, from €212 in May, and Gramacho to €95, from €155.

See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in June

From June onwards, the west of the Algarve is noticeably cooler than the centre and east: about three degrees cooler in the afternoon on average, with far fewer hot days. If you don't enjoy playing in the heat, courses near Lagos and Sagres, such as Santo António, Espiche and [Boavista](/courses/boavista), are a good choice, and they're among the cheapest in our table too. Inland courses tend to be hotter than the coast. Read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf) to compare the two ends of the region.
Crowds and what else is on in June

Golf traffic thins out through June as the weather warms up, so tee times are easier to find than in spring. Hotels go the other way: rooms fill up and prices rise as the beach season begins, so you may pay less for your golf and more for your hotel than in April.
10 June is Portugal Day, a national holiday, and June is the month of the popular saints' festivals in Portuguese towns, with street parties and grilled sardines.
Frequently asked questions
Is June a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, if you're happy to play early or late in the day. It's warm and dry, the days are the longest of the year, and green fees fall to low-season levels on many courses.
Is it too hot to play golf in the Algarve in June?

Not usually. The average high in Faro is about 27°C, with around five days above 30°C in the month. The west is cooler, at around 24°C. Play early in the morning or late in the afternoon and drink plenty of water.
Does it rain in the Algarve in June?
Very rarely. Faro averages 5 mm of rain in June, and less than one rainy day.
What time does it get light and dark in the Algarve in June?
The sun rises at about 6.15am and sets between about 8.45pm and 8.55pm, which gives you almost 15 hours of daylight for golf.

algarve-golf-in-july.text: Is July a good month for golf in the Algarve? It's hot, but it can be very good value. Afternoons average about **29°C** in Faro, it hardly ever rains, and green fees are at or near their lowest of the year: on 14 of the 29 courses we track, July shares the lowest price. The secret is to play early or late, and to pick your courses with the heat in mind.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in July from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where it's cooler.

The far west is much cooler: Sagres averages just over 25°C, with only two or three days above 30°C. Rain is almost non-existent, at about 1 mm in the whole month.
What July weather means on the course
**Fairways and greens.** The courses are irrigated and stay green, but fairways are hard and fast in July and the ball runs a long way. Greens can be firm and a little slower than in spring.

**Tee times.** Play at dawn or in the evening. A tee time between about 7am and 8.30am will have you finished before the worst of the heat, and with sunset after 8.40pm, a 4.30pm start still gets you round in daylight. Avoid the middle of the day if you can: it's hard on your body and your scorecard.

**What to pack.** Lightweight, breathable golf clothes, a wide-brimmed hat, sunglasses and high-factor sun cream. Carry at least a litre of water for a round, and take a buggy if you're playing anywhere near midday.
Green fees in July

July is summer low season for golf in the Algarve. On 14 of the 29 courses we track, July shares the lowest price of the year, and on average fees are about **34% below** each course's peak, the joint biggest saving of any month. Amendoeira's Faldo Course costs €109, against €212 in spring, and Quinta do Lago South €188, against €264.

Where to play in July: head west to stay cool

In July, where you play makes a real difference to the heat. Sagres, at the western tip, averages about 25°C against more than 29°C in Faro, and has about three days above 30°C in the month against 13. The western courses around Lagos and Sagres, such as Santo António, Espiche and [Boavista](/courses/boavista), are also among the cheapest in our table. Crowds and what else is on in July

Courses are quiet in July, because most visitors are on the beach rather than the fairway, so you can usually find tee times at short notice. Hotels are the opposite: July is high season, with UK, Irish and Portuguese school holidays overlapping in the second half of the month, so book your accommodation well ahead and expect higher room rates.
Frequently asked questions
Is July a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, if you can handle the heat and play early or late. Courses are quiet and green fees are among the lowest of the year, but hotels are at their busiest and most expensive.
Is it too hot to play golf in the Algarve in July?

It can be in the middle of the day. Faro averages 29°C in July, with about 13 days above 30°C. Tee off before 8.30am or after about 4.30pm, carry plenty of water, and consider the cooler west, where Sagres averages about 25°C.
Does it rain in the Algarve in July?
Almost never. Faro averages about 1 mm of rain in the whole of July.
What time does it get light and dark in the Algarve in July?
The sun rises between about 6.15am and 6.35am and sets between about 8.40pm and 8.55pm, giving you around 14 and a half hours of daylight.

Afternoons average about **29°C** in Faro, it barely rains, and green fees are at their summer low: on 14 of the 29 courses we track, August shares the lowest price of the year. Play early or late, and the courses are yours.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in August from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where it's cooler.
Algarve weather in August for golf

**Fairways and greens.** Irrigated courses stay green through August, but the fairways are hard and fast, and you'll get lots of roll off the tee. Firm greens reward a lower, running approach.

Late-afternoon rounds work too, but with sunset moving earlier, a start around 4pm is about the latest for 18 holes by the end of the month.

**What to pack.** Lightweight, breathable clothes, a wide-brimmed hat, sunglasses and high-factor sun cream. Carry plenty of water, and take a buggy for any round that runs into the middle of the day.
Green fees in August

August is summer low season for golf. On 14 of the 29 courses we track, August shares the lowest green fee of the year, and on average fees are about **34% below** each course's peak. The savings at the big-name courses are large: Gramacho costs €95 against €180 in spring, and Amendoeira's Faldo Course €109 against €212.

algarve-golf-in-september.text: Is September a good month for golf in the Algarve? Many golfers think it's the best month of the year. The summer heat eases to an average high of about **26°C**, rain falls on only about two days, and the courses get quieter once the school holidays end. Green fees are heading back up, though: on average they're only about 12% below each course's peak.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in September from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where to play.
Algarve weather in September for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

algarve-golf-in-september.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunrise and sunset are calculated for the first and last day of September, in Portuguese summer time (the same as UK time).

algarve-golf-in-september.text: September is still summer in the Algarve, but a gentler one. The average high in Faro is about 26°C, with around three days above 30°C, and Sagres averages about 25°C. Mornings are warm, at around 18°C. Rain returns, but only just: about 22 mm in Faro over two days. The days shorten by more than an hour over the month.
What September weather means on the course
**Fairways and greens.** Courses come out of the summer firm and fast, and generally in good condition. Expect plenty of roll off the tee and firm greens, especially early in the month.

**Tee times.** The heat is less of a problem than in July and August, so mid-morning tee times become comfortable again. To finish 18 holes in daylight, tee off by about 3.30pm in early September and by about 3pm at the end of the month.
**What to pack.** Summer golf kit: light, breathable clothes, a cap, sunglasses and sun cream. A light layer for early starts at the end of the month, and a small umbrella just in case.
Green fees in September

September is when green fees climb back towards their autumn peak. On average they're about **12% below** each course's highest price, against about a third below in July and August, and on 6 of the 30 courses we track September is already at the year's top rate. Amendoeira's Faldo Course, for example, goes from €109 in August to €197 in September.

Where to play in September

Crowds and what else is on in September

The beach crowds thin out once UK schools go back at the start of September, and hotel prices generally ease from their August peak. The golf season goes the other way: autumn golf groups start to arrive through the month, so tee sheets get busier towards the end of September. Book ahead for the second half of the month.
Frequently asked questions
Is September a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, it's one of the best months: warm but not too hot, very little rain, firm courses and quieter beaches. Green fees are rising towards their autumn peak, so it isn't as cheap as summer.
Is it still hot in the Algarve in September?
Warm rather than hot. The average high is about 26°C in Faro and 25°C in Sagres, with around three days above 30°C in Faro.
Does it rain in the Algarve in September?
Not much. Faro averages 22 mm of rain in September over about two rainy days, and Sagres 19 mm over two or three.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in September?

algarve-golf-in-october.text: Is October a good month for golf in the Algarve? Yes, it's the heart of the autumn golf season. Afternoons average about **23°C**, early October can still feel like summer, and the courses are in good shape. The trade-offs are the return of the rain, about six rainy days on average, and the price: October is autumn peak season, and fees are only about 8% below each course's highest rate on average.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in October from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and what changes when the clocks go back.
Algarve weather in October for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

algarve-golf-in-october.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of October, in Portuguese local time; the clocks go back an hour on the last Sunday of October, as in the UK, which moves sunset from about 6.40pm to 5.40pm.
algarve-golf-in-october.caption: October weather in the Algarve

algarve-golf-in-october.text: October is warm, with an average high of about 23°C in Faro and 22°C in Sagres, and mornings around 16°C. It's also the month the rain comes back: Faro averages 56 mm over about six days, with about two days of heavy rain, and Sagres a little more. In an average October, Faro still has about seven days of 25°C or more.
What October weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** Courses are generally in good condition in October. After the first heavy rain, fairways soften and the ball stops running so far. Some clubs carry out autumn maintenance around this time, so it's worth asking about course conditions when you book.

**Tee times.** Until the clocks go back on the last Sunday of October, tee off by about 2.30pm to 3pm to finish 18 holes in daylight. After the change, sunset moves to about 5.40pm and the latest sensible tee time to about 1.30pm.
**What to pack.** Short sleeves for most afternoons, a light jumper for the mornings and a waterproof jacket and umbrella for the showers. Sun cream is still essential.
Green fees in October

October is the Algarve's autumn peak for golf. On 10 of the 30 courses we track, October is at the year's highest price, and on average fees are only about **8% below** each course's peak. There are some savings at the very top end: Monte Rei costs €245 in October against €312 in spring.

algarve-golf-in-october.note: The lowest price any visitor can book for one 18-hole round, from each club's official price list or its own online booking, checked in October 2026. All year shows the course's cheapest and dearest months. Prices change, so check before you book.

algarve-golf-in-october.text: Twilight rounds help keep costs down: this October they start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves). Remember that the daylight runs out faster after the clocks go back. See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in October

Temperatures are similar across the region in October, and the west gets slightly more rain than the centre and east, so pick your base for the courses. The cheapest courses in our table this month are in the far west and east, with Santo António at €68 and Espiche at €90. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Crowds, half-term and the clock change

October is one of the busiest months on the Algarve's courses, as golfers from northern Europe arrive for the autumn season. Book tee times and hotels as early as you can, especially for morning slots at the best-known courses. The UK's October half-term falls in the last week or so of the month, adding families to the mix.

The clocks go back on the last Sunday of October, the same day as in the UK, so there's no time difference to worry about, but sunset jumps an hour earlier overnight. 5 October is a public holiday in Portugal.
Frequently asked questions
Is October a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, it's one of the most popular months: warm afternoons, courses in good shape and plenty of daylight until the clocks change. It's peak season, though, so prices are high and tee times book up.
Is it still warm in the Algarve in October?
Yes. The average high is about 23°C in Faro and 22°C in Sagres, and early October can still feel like summer.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in October?
Faro averages 56 mm of rain in October over about six rainy days, and Sagres 61 mm over about seven, with about two days of heavy rain.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in October?
The sun sets at about 7.15pm at the start of October and about 6.40pm just before the clocks go back. After the change, on the last Sunday of the month, sunset is around 5.40pm.

algarve-golf-in-november.text: Is November a good month for golf in the Algarve? It's a good-value month if you're flexible about the weather. Afternoons still average about **20°C**, but November is one of the wettest months of the year, with about seven rainy days in Faro, and the days are short, with sunset between about 5.15pm and 5.35pm. Green fees start to fall: on 7 of the 29 courses we track, November shares the lowest price of the year.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in November from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay and where to play.
Algarve weather in November for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. Faro represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight is for the middle of the month; sunset is calculated for the first and last day of November, in Portuguese winter time (the same as UK time).
algarve-golf-in-november.caption: November weather in the Algarve

algarve-golf-in-november.text: November is mild: the average high is about 20°C in Faro and 19°C in Sagres, and mornings are around 12°C. It's also when the Algarve's rainy season gets going. Faro averages 76 mm over about seven days, and Sagres 82 mm over about eight, making November the wettest month of the year in the far west. The rain usually comes with Atlantic fronts, so a wet spell of a few days is often followed by a run of clear, calm weather.
What November weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** After the first heavy autumn rain, fairways soften and play longer, and some clubs restrict buggies to the paths after a downpour. Greens are receptive and hold approach shots well.
**Tee times.** With about ten hours of daylight and sunset around 5.20pm, tee off by about 1pm to finish 18 holes. Late morning is the most pleasant time to start.

**What to pack.** Layers: short sleeves may still do on a sunny afternoon, but bring a jumper and a good waterproof jacket and trousers. An umbrella, a spare glove and waterproof golf shoes are worth packing in November.
Green fees in November

November is when green fees start to come down after the autumn peak. On 7 of the 29 courses we track, November shares the lowest price of the year, and on average fees are about **17% below** each course's peak. Some courses drop sharply: Monte Rei costs €190 in November against €312 in spring, and the Vilamoura Laguna and Millennium courses are both under €100.

algarve-golf-in-november.text: This November twilight rounds start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and €55 at Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves). With the light going early, check the start time when you book. See also [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in November

Temperatures are almost the same across the region in November, but the west is wetter: Sagres averages about two more rainy days than Faro. If the forecast is unsettled, the centre and east may give you a slightly better chance of dry rounds. The Vilamoura courses are good value this month, with [Vilamoura Laguna](/courses/vilamoura-laguna) at €88 and [Millennium](/courses/vilamoura-millennium) at €92. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Crowds and what else is on in November

The courses quieten down through November after the busy autumn season, and tee times get easier to find, especially later in the month. Hotels are generally cheaper too, but some seasonal resort hotels close for part of the winter, so check that yours is open on your dates. 1 November is a public holiday in Portugal.
Frequently asked questions
Is November a good time to play golf in the Algarve?
Yes, if you're flexible about the weather. Afternoons are still mild, the courses are quieter than in October and green fees are starting to fall. Expect about seven rainy days and short afternoons.
Is the Algarve warm in November?
Mild. The average high is about 20°C in Faro and 19°C in Sagres, with mornings around 12°C.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in November?
Faro averages 76 mm of rain in November over about seven rainy days, and Sagres 82 mm over about eight. In the far west, November is the wettest month of the year.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in November?
The sun sets at about 5.35pm at the start of November and about 5.15pm at the end. Tee off by about 1pm to finish 18 holes in daylight.

algarve-golf-in-december.text: Is December a good month for golf in the Algarve? For most golfers, yes. Afternoons reach about **17°C**, frost is virtually unknown on the coast, and it's the **cheapest month of the year** to play on 26 of the 29 courses we track. The catch is that December is also the Algarve's wettest month on average, and the days are short, with the sun setting at around 5.15pm.
This guide covers the Algarve weather in December from a golfer's point of view: what the numbers mean on the course, when to tee off, what you'll pay, and what changes around Christmas.
Algarve weather in December for golf

The figures below are the official 1991–2020 climate averages from IPMA, Portugal's national weather service. We show two stations: Faro, which represents the central and eastern Algarve, where most of the courses are, and Sagres, at the western tip near [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio).

algarve-golf-in-december.note: Source: IPMA climate normals 1991–2020 for Faro (station 554) and Sagres (station 533), averaged over 30 years. Rainy days have 1 mm of rain or more; heavy rain days 10 mm or more. Daylight and sunset are calculated for 1 to 31 December, in Portuguese winter time (the same as UK time).
algarve-golf-in-december.caption: December weather in the Algarve

algarve-golf-in-december.text: The headline is that the temperature hardly changes across the region: whether you're in Lagos, Vilamoura or Tavira, expect afternoons in the mid to high teens and mornings around 10°C. Rain is the variable. December averages around seven rainy days, which leaves roughly three weeks of dry golf, but the rain tends to arrive with Atlantic fronts that can bring two or three wet days in a row. Only about three days in the month see heavy rain.
What December weather means on the course

**Fairways and greens.** After a wet spell, fairways soften and you'll get less roll off the tee, so the courses play a little longer than they do in summer. Some clubs keep buggies on the paths after heavy rain to protect the turf, which means more walking to your ball. On the plus side, the courses are green and receptive, and approach shots hold the greens.

**Tee times.** With under ten hours of daylight and the sun down by about 5.20pm, timing matters more than temperature. A four-hour round needs a tee time no later than about 1pm, and in practice late morning is the sweet spot: the dew has burned off, the air has warmed up and you'll finish in daylight. Early starts are possible, but expect cold hands and wet grass before 9am.

**What to pack.** Layers rather than a heavy coat: a base layer and a windproof or waterproof top that you can take off as the afternoon warms up. Bring a proper waterproof jacket and trousers, an umbrella and a spare glove, and waterproof golf shoes are worth more than usual in December. Sun cream still earns its place on a clear day.

**Rain plans.** If a front comes through, the forecast usually gives you a day or two of warning, so keep your bookings flexible and play the dry days. And if it's dark by half past five, Amendoeira has the only floodlit nine-hole course in Portugal, according to the resort: see [night golf in the Algarve](/guide/night-golf-in-the-algarve).
Green fees in December: the cheapest month of the year

This is where December really pays off. On 26 of the 29 courses we track, December has the lowest green fee of the year, and on average December fees are about **34% below** each course's peak price. The savings are biggest at the courses that charge most in spring and autumn.

algarve-golf-in-december.text: Some clubs also sell cheaper twilight rounds. Twilight rates this December start from €35 at Santo António and €50 at Alto Golf, and Pestana's [Gramacho](/courses/gramacho), [Vale da Pinta](/courses/vale-da-pinta) and [Silves](/courses/silves) courses offer them at €55. A late twilight slot in December won't give you 18 holes before dark, so check the start time when you book.

Salgados, near Albufeira, puts December in its low season on its official 2026 price list, at €91 for 18 holes. For the full picture of where to play for less all year round, see [the cheapest golf courses in the Algarve](/guide/the-cheapest-golf-courses-in-the-algarve).
Where to play in December

Because December is the low season almost everywhere, it's the best month of the year to play the Algarve's big-name courses for less. Amendoeira's Faldo Course costs less than half its spring price, and Quinta do Lago and Monte Rei are around €70 to €120 cheaper than at peak. If there's one premium round on your wish list, December is the time to book it.

East or west makes little difference to the weather this month: the western tip around Sagres sees slightly more rainy days, while Faro gets more rain in total, and temperatures are almost identical. Pick your base for the courses rather than the climate. If you're weighing up the two ends of the region, read [West vs East Algarve: which side is better for golf?](/guide/west-vs-east-algarve-which-side-is-better-for-golf).
Christmas, New Year and crowds

Most of December is quiet on the fairways. Tee sheets are open, you can often book a day or two ahead, and rounds tend to flow without long waits. The exception is the fortnight around Christmas and New Year, when UK school holidays bring families and groups out, so book ahead if you're travelling in the last two weeks of the month.

Almost every course in the Algarve sells December tee times, but opening hours on Christmas Day and New Year's Day vary from club to club, so check with the course before you plan a festive round. The same goes for hotels: prices are low, but some seasonal resort hotels close for part of the winter, so check your hotel is open on your dates.
Frequently asked questions
Is December a good time to play golf in the Algarve?

Yes, if you want low prices and quiet courses and you're happy to play around the odd wet day. Afternoons average about 17°C, frost is very rare on the coast and green fees are at their lowest of the year on most courses. The trade-offs are short days and the highest average rainfall of the year in Faro.
Is it warm enough to play golf in the Algarve in December?

Yes. The average daily high is 17°C in both Faro and Sagres, and the average low is around 10°C. Most golfers play in a long-sleeved top or a light jumper, adding a waterproof layer when the weather turns.
How much does it rain in the Algarve in December?

Faro averages 90 mm of rain in December over about seven rainy days, and Sagres 75 mm over about eight. On most other days of the month there's no meaningful rain, but wet spells can last two or three days.
What time does it get dark in the Algarve in December?
The sun sets at around 5.15pm to 5.30pm throughout December, and rises at about 7.30am to 7.50am. To finish 18 holes in daylight, aim to tee off by about 1pm.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: The best place to stay for golf in the Algarve depends on how many courses you want to play and what you want from your evenings. If golf comes first, **Vilamoura, Quarteira and the Golden Triangle around Almancil** put the most courses within a short drive, and they are the closest bases to Faro Airport. **Albufeira** suits groups who want nightlife, **Carvoeiro and Tavira** are quieter, and **Lagos and Alvor** are the bases for the western courses, where green fees are often lower.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: The numbers show why golfers keep coming back to the central Algarve: from Almancil, nine courses are within about 15 minutes. In the far west and east there are fewer courses close together, but they are usually cheaper and quieter. Summer traffic on the coast road can add a lot to these times, so in July and August allow extra.
Which base suits your trip?
You want to play as many courses as possible

Stay in **Vilamoura, Quarteira or Almancil**. From Quarteira, 7 courses are within about 15 minutes, including the four Vilamoura Golf courses, Pestana Vila Sol and the two Vale do Lobo courses, and 14 are within half an hour. See [golf near Quarteira](/quarteira/golf-courses) and the [Vilamoura golf courses](/vilamoura/golf-courses).
Luxury and the best-known courses

Stay in the **Golden Triangle**, the area between Almancil, Quinta do Lago and Vale do Lobo. It has the Algarve's best-known courses, including [Quinta do Lago South](/courses/quinta-do-lago-south) and the clifftop holes of [Vale do Lobo Royal](/courses/vale-do-lobo-royal), and five-star hotels and resort villas. Expect some of the highest green fees in the region: Quinta do Lago South starts at €188. See the [hotels near Quinta do Lago](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-do-lago-golf) and [hotels near Vale do Lobo](/guide/hotels-near-vale-do-lobo-golf).
A golf trip on a budget

Look west to **Lagos and Praia da Luz**, or east to **Tavira**. Around Lagos, [Santo António](/courses/santo-antonio) starts at €57, [Espiche](/courses/espiche) at €65 and [Boavista](/courses/boavista) at €74. In the east, [Benamor](/courses/benamor) starts at €66 and [Quinta do Vale](/courses/quinta-do-vale) at €67. You'll have fewer courses within a short drive, so plan two or three rounds rather than six. Our guide to [the best-value golf in the Algarve](/guide/best-value-golf-in-the-algarve) has more ideas.
A short break or a weekend

Stay close to the airport. Almancil and Vilamoura are around 30–35 minutes from Faro Airport, so you can play on the day you land. [Faro](/faro/golf-courses) itself has no course, but Quinta do Lago Laranjal is about 20 minutes from the city. Our [golf weekend in the Algarve](/guide/golf-weekend-in-the-algarve) guide plans three nights and two rounds from four different bases.
Nightlife and group trips

**Albufeira** is the Algarve's party town. Its nightlife is centred on "the Strip", Avenida Sá Carneiro in the Montechoro area, about 3 km east of the old town. The closest courses are [Balaia](/courses/balaia), about 15 minutes away, and [Salgados](/courses/salgados) and [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs), about 20, with the Vilamoura courses around 25. If you'd rather have restaurants and bars than clubs, **Vilamoura's marina** is busy in the evenings and has a casino. For tips on organising a society or a group, read [golf trips for groups](/guide/algarve-golf-trips-for-groups-and-golf-societies).
Peace and quiet

**Tavira** is a historic town on the river Gilão and is much quieter than the central resorts, with [Benamor](/courses/benamor) about 15 minutes away and the two Quinta da Ria courses about 20. **Carvoeiro** is a small cliffside village with Gramacho, Vale da Pinta and Vale de Milho all within about 15 minutes. **Praia da Luz** is a small resort west of Lagos, about 10 minutes from Boavista.
Golfers with non-golfing partners, families or beginners

Pick a base with a short course that needs no handicap certificate, so everyone can play. [Pine Cliffs](/courses/pine-cliffs) (9 holes) is next to [Olhos de Água](/olhos-de-agua/golf-courses), the 9-hole [Penina Resort](/courses/penina-resort) course is about 15 minutes from [Alvor](/alvor/golf-courses), and [Vale de Milho](/courses/vale-de-milho), a 9-hole par-3 course, is in Carvoeiro. [Balaia](/courses/balaia), another 9-hole par-3 course near Albufeira, does ask for a handicap. For lessons, see the [Algarve golf academies](/golf-academies).
Without a car

The easiest way is to stay at a resort with its own course, so the first tee is a walk away: see our list of [Algarve hotels with a golf course on site](/guide/algarve-hotels-with-a-golf-course-on-site). The train line along the coast stops in the centre of Lagos, Faro and Tavira, but Albufeira's station is several kilometres outside the town, and most courses are a taxi ride from the nearest station. For getting from the airport, see [Faro Airport to the Algarve golf courses](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses).
The bases one by one
A few well-rated hotels in each base, all checked for our other hotel guides. Prices are the lowest we found for a recent date and change with the season, so check your own dates.
Vilamoura and Quarteira

Vilamoura is built around its marina, with the four Vilamoura Golf courses and Pestana Vila Sol all within about 15 minutes. Quarteira, its beach-town neighbour, is just as close to the courses. From Vilamoura's marina, 13 courses are within 30 minutes. More in [golf near Quarteira](/quarteira/golf-courses) and [golf hotels near Vilamoura](/guide/golf-hotels-near-vilamoura).

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: Carvoeiro and Armação de Pêra

Carvoeiro is a small cliffside village, with Gramacho, Vale da Pinta and the 9-hole Vale de Milho all within about 15 minutes and Pestana Ferragudo about 15–20. A little further east, Armação de Pêra is the closest town to Salgados and Amendoeira. More in [golf near Armação de Pêra](/armacao-de-pera/golf-courses) and [hotels near Vale de Milho](/guide/hotels-near-vale-de-milho-golf).

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Pestana Palm Gardens
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: Clifftop studios and apartments in Carvoeiro run by Pestana, the same group that owns Ferragudo. Pestana says guests get **exclusive benefits and discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta**, so it is a smart base if you want to play all three Pestana courses. Breakfast starts at 8am and is charged separately, but every unit has a kitchen, so an early bite before your round is easy.
perks: Discounts at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Tivoli Carvoeiro Algarve Resort
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A five-star clifftop resort a short walk from Carvoeiro village, rated **8.6 on Booking.com**, with sea views, a full spa and indoor and outdoor pools. UK golf tour operators sell packages here that include rounds at Gramacho and Vale da Pinta.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Vila Vita Parc
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A clifftop resort near Porches rated an exceptional **9.5 on Booking.com**, from about €246 a night in October. It's 15 minutes from Salgados and 18 from Amendoeira. Pick it if the weekend is a special occasion rather than just a golf trip.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: Portimão and Alvor

Portimão and Alvor are the bases for the Sir Henry Cotton courses: [Alto Golf](/courses/alto-golf) is about 5 minutes from both, and [Penina](/courses/penina-championship) about 15–20. Pestana Ferragudo is about 15 minutes from Portimão, Gramacho and Vale da Pinta about 20, Morgado about 25 and Álamos about 30. More in [golf near Alvor](/alvor/golf-courses) and [hotels near Penina](/guide/hotels-near-penina-golf-resort).

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Jupiter Marina Hotel
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A stylish hotel on Portimão marina, with a spa, a rooftop bar and a free shuttle to Praia da Rocha beach. It scores **9.0 on Booking.com**, unusually high for the price, and breakfast starts at 7.30am. Parking is paid.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: RR Alvor Baía Resort
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A large, family-friendly resort of suites with kitchenettes, with a spa, gym and heated hydrotherapy pool. For golfers the useful detail is breakfast: it starts at 7am, and the hotel offers **a breakfast pack for early-morning departures** if you ask at reception the day before, ideal for a first tee time at Penina.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Penina Hotel & Golf Resort
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: The Algarve's original golf resort, with the 18-hole Championship and the 9-hole Resort course on site. The Championship course was designed by Sir Henry Cotton. Penina's "Best Available Rate for Golfers" includes **a complimentary round every day** on one of its courses (a handicap certificate is needed for the Championship course). Breakfast starts at 7am.
perks: Free daily round on the golfer rate

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: Lagos and Praia da Luz

Lagos has a lively old town and a marina, with Boavista about 10 minutes away and Palmares and Espiche about 20. Praia da Luz is quieter and closer to Boavista, Espiche and Santo António. Green fees here are among the lowest in the Algarve, but Vilamoura and Quinta do Lago are about an hour away. More in [golf near Praia da Luz](/praia-da-luz/golf-courses) and [hotels near Boavista](/guide/hotels-near-boavista-golf).

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Hotel Marina Rio
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A four-star hotel opposite Lagos marina, a short walk from the old town, rated **9.0 on Booking.com** from more than 1,000 reviews. A private garage is available if you reserve in advance. About 9 minutes from Boavista.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Belavista da Luz
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A four-star wellness hotel in Praia da Luz, rated **8.5 on Booking.com** from more than 1,000 reviews, with a spa. About 8 minutes from Boavista.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Palmares Beach House Hotel
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: The five-star boutique hotel on the Palmares resort, adults only, with just 20 rooms including two suites. It scores **8.9 on Booking.com**, and Palmares sells Stay & Play packages that combine a stay with rounds on its 27 holes. Right at Palmares.
Tavira and the east

Tavira is the base for the eastern courses: Benamor about 15 minutes away, Quinta da Ria and Quinta de Cima about 20, and Quinta do Vale and Castro Marim about 25–30. Monte Rei, the Jack Nicklaus course, is about 35 minutes from Tavira and closer to Monte Gordo. More in [golf near Monte Gordo](/monte-gordo/golf-courses) and [hotels near Quinta da Ria](/guide/hotels-near-quinta-da-ria-golf).

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Hotel Don Rodrigues
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A small hotel rated **8.8 on Booking.com**, from €65 a night **with breakfast** on its own website. It has an outdoor pool and free parking, and it's 12 minutes from Benamor. Breakfast starts at 8am, so for an early tee time ask about something to take with you.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: OZADI Tavira Hotel
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A four-star hotel on the edge of Tavira, rated **9.0 on Booking.com** from more than 3,700 reviews and from about €77 a night in November. Benamor is about 6 minutes away, and it has two pools and free parking.

where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.name: Pousada Convento Tavira
where-to-stay-in-the-algarve-for-golf.text: A Pousada in a former 16th-century convent in the centre of Tavira, rated **9.0 on Booking.com** and from €131 a night on its own website. You can walk to the old town's restaurants after the round. Breakfast runs from 8am to 11am.
Faro

Faro is the Algarve's capital and the airport is on the edge of the city, but there is no golf course in Faro itself. It works for a night before an early flight or a short city break with a round at [Quinta do Lago Laranjal](/courses/quinta-do-lago-laranjal), about 20 minutes away. For hotels in the city, see [golf near Faro](/faro/golf-courses).
Plan the rest of your trip

Once you've picked a base, compare green fees in the [full list of Algarve golf courses](/courses), check [how to get from Faro Airport to your base with clubs](/guide/faro-airport-to-algarve-golf-courses), and if you're not bringing your own set, read our [club rental guide](/club-rental).
